title: Cycle-Tracking Apps Bring Substantial Risks to Users, New Analysis Finds
snippet: This includes apps that promote the practice of cycle syncing.
fullText:
It’s been estimated that about 50 million people worldwide use apps to track their menstrual cycles, associated mental and physical symptoms, fertility and pregnancy. However, a new analysis published in the peer-reviewed medical journal The BMJ on Wednesday argues that the risks associated with these apps and other digital cycle-tracking tools on the femtech market do more harm than good. 

The authors of the article say that these risks extend to digital menstrual cycle-tracking tools that promote “cycle syncing,” which is when one bases their diet, exercise and other lifestyle habits on their menstrual cycle phases. 

“We hope that people understand a lot of the big, splashy claims around cycle tracking and cycle syncing that people encounter on social media or in fitness or wellness spaces are not based on scientific evidence,” Katharine Lee, one of the article’s authors and an assistant professor in Tulane University’s Department of Anthropology, told CNET in an email. 

			

More from CNET

The health risks

Drawing on several studies, the analysis states that sports science research has shown there is no way to generalize about how different menstrual cycle phases affect health, performance or injury risk. These correlations are highly individual. The same goes for research on how diet can reduce cycle symptoms or improve performance, which is generally inconclusive or speculative.  

Even if these cycle connections did exist, the article argues that digital cycle-tracking tools wouldn’t be able to predict them. Apps tend to rely on a user’s self-reported menstrual bleeding date to estimate ovulation, the fertile window and future menstrual cycle phases. Without actually measuring someone’s hormones, these estimates can be imprecise, especially considering that hormones and ovulation fluctuate.

Digital menstrual cycle trackers also can’t diagnose menstrual disorders or uncover the causes of painful periods. 

“You should work with trusted health professionals if you have concerns — and yes, I know that many people struggle to get their doctors to listen to them about their periods,” Lee said. “People may want to track their cycles for any number of reasons, but a lot of digital tracking apps are no fancier than counting and averaging your data.”

When relying on these apps, there’s a risk that users may downplay health concerns as simply effects of their cycle. Or forgo established diet, exercise and sleep guidelines in the name of cycle syncing. 

Privacy isn’t the only concern when using an app to track your cycle.SeventyFour/Getty Images

The privacy problem

There’s also privacy to consider, as some apps allow third-party tracking, don’t publish transparency reports, don’t allow straightforward data deletion and don’t use local data storage, which makes it easier for them to sell data, share it with third parties or be exposed to a data breach. This is especially dangerous in areas where abortion is criminalized or where there is more gender or sex-based discrimination.

While no specific apps or tools were mentioned in this analysis, Lee said that several of the cited references focus on the policies or functionality of specific apps. 

Magnifying gender inequities

Despite being used by and promoted to millions, the article states that evidence supporting these tools’ ability to help manage people’s menstrual cycles and overall health is lacking. 

These apps also aren’t the solution to gender inequities in healthcare or in the world as a whole. Instead, they put people’s health and privacy at risk while wasting their time and compounding existing inequities around access to safety, rest, nutrition, healthcare and menstrual supplies. This is especially poignant considering that many cycle-tracking apps use the language of women’s empowerment in their marketing. 

How should you track your cycle?

There’s no single best way to track your cycle, especially since tracking methods should be tailored to individual concerns. 

For instance, according to Lee, if someone is concerned about fertility, they should ensure they track signs of ovulation, including basal body temperature, cervical mucus consistency and luteinizing hormone levels. When managing health conditions such as endometriosis, migraines or premenopausal dysphoric disorder, which can vary with menstrual cycles, monitoring the associated symptoms and predicting the next estimated time of bleeding may be more important than focusing on ovulation. 

“Most apps can’t detect ovulation or determine what phase someone is in based just on bleeding,” Lee said. “Even if these simple apps could detect ovulation and cycle phase, there are no generalizable trends in what people experience across the cycle.”

If you choose to track your cycle with an app, make sure you look into its privacy policy. Lee specifically shared research conducted by the nonprofit Mozilla Foundation, which aims to build a better tech future, and by Privacy International, a London-based charity focused on worldwide privacy protection. You could also use your digital calendar or avoid digital tracking entirely by opting for a pen and paper.

“It’s really important that people understand the potential risks [of digital menstrual tracking], including the possibility of reproductive coercion and if you live somewhere where abortion is criminalized,” Lee said. “It’s already gross enough that some apps share period data with companies to send you targeted advertising, but the safety of your information can be a real concern for many people.”

Over the past 12 years, Anna has also written for the LA Times, Elle, Bust Magazine, Dazed, Apartment Therapy, Well+Good and more. title: DoorDash now lets you order by text in Apple Messages
snippet: DoorDash today launched a new way to order your next meal: via text in Apple’s Messages app, powered by AI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
DoorDash today launched a new way to order your next meal: via text in Apple’s Messages app, powered by AI. Here are the details.

DoorDash text ordering launches on iPhone, powered by AI agent

AI agents are here to stay, and they don’t just look like cute digital creatures. While Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots have gotten a lot of attention, AI agents are popping up in ways that are less obviously “AI” too.

For example, today DoorDash launched the ability to skip the app and simply text to place your food order in Apple’s Messages app. It’s available in the US only to start, and interested users will need to first join this waitlist. And it’s all powered by an AI agent.

Here’s the rundown on how it works, via DoorDash’s announcement:

Text what you’re craving: Ask for a specific dish, request a local recommendation based on your mood, or simply reorder your go-to Friday night meal for the family.

Skip the search: DoorDash searches local spots, scans menus, and suggests a cart based on what you’re in the mood for. It even texts you photos of the food it recommends right from the restaurant’s store page on the DoorDash app. 

Truly personalized ordering: Text “order my usual” and it knows you mean your Friday night order — no need to spell out the dish, the modifiers, or the restaurant. It already knows whether you skip cilantro, always add extra sauce, or never miss dessert. The more you order, the more it learns, and if you want, it can message you proactively to ask if you want your usual coffee order based on your daily habits.

Manage group preferences with ease: Ordering for large groups is never easy, especially when everyone wants something different. It can handle mixed dietary preferences and different quantities in one order, so you’re not the one juggling everyone’s requests.

Checkout without ever opening the app: Confirm your order right inside the text thread and it manages checkout.

To get started, join DoorDash’s waitlist and you’ll be notified when text access is granted. Depending on demand, that access might arrive right away, or it may take some time.

Are you interested in using DoorDash’s AI agent to order via Apple’s Messages app? Let us know in the comments.

The monthly “Google System Release Notes” primarily detail what’s new in Play services, Play Store, and Play system update across Android phones/tablets, Wear OS, Google/Android TV, Auto, and PC. Some features apply to end users, while others are aimed at developers.

The following first-party apps comprise the “Google System”:

Android AICore: Search the “All apps” list in Settings and open App info for the version number

Adaptive Connectivity Services: App info

Android Developer Verifier: App info

Android Pulse: App info

Android System Intelligence: App info

Android System Key Verifier: App info

Android System SafetyCore: App info

Android System WebView: App info

Android TV Core Services

Device Health Services: App info

Google Partner Setup: App info

Google Play Protect Service: App info

Google Play services: App info

Google Play Services for AR: App info

Google Play Store: App info

Google Play system update: Settings > About phone > Android version

Private Compute Services: App info

Quick Share Extension: App info

Search Engine Selector: App info

Settings Services: App info

SIM Manager: App info

System parental controls: App info

To update, open the Settings app > tap your name at the very top for “Google services” (on Pixel) > All services tab > Privacy & security > System services.

A feature appearing in the changelog does not mean it’s widely available. Some capabilities take months to fully launch.

	

Google Play services v26.38 (2026-09-28)

Account Management

[Auto] You can now sign in to your Google Account directly within the setup flow when you get started with Gemini in your vehicle.

Developer Services

[Phone] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Maps related processes in their apps.

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Analytics & Diagnostics related processes in their apps.

Support

[Phone] You’ll now get new features for Gemini, Circle to Search, Quick Share, Find Hub, and Android Auto.

Google Play Store v53.4 (2026-09-28)

[Phone] Removed the “Users are saying” header above the review paragraph summaries in the Details Page Rating & Review section.

Android WebView v155 (2026-09-23)

Refactored the androidx.webkit Navigation and NavigationListener APIs to be thread safe.

Improvements to security and privacy and updates for bug fixes.

New developer features for Google & 3rd party app developers to support functionality related to displaying web content in their apps.

Important: Some features may be experimental and available to certain users.

Related: Google rolls out Motion Assist bubbles to Pixel, Samsung

Google Play services v26.37 (2026-09-21)

Health & Fitness

[Wear] With this update, you’ll get improvements and bug fixes for real-time metric data sent from your watch to your phone.

Safety & Emergency

[Phone] With this update, Motion assist can help mitigate motion sickness with subtle, visual shapes that move in sync with a vehicle’s motion.

[Phone] With this update, you can more easily find the Driving Do Not Disturb feature.

System Management

[Phone] Updates to system management services that improve Device Performance and Stability.

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] This update adds support for larger and more refined system emoji font downloads.

Google Play Store v53.3 (2026-09-21)

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] You can now make purchases in local currency in Argentina, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, and Ethiopia.

[Wear] This update includes changes to the search results page.

[Phone] You can add a pre-registered paid title to your wishlist once it’s published.

Google Play services v26.36 (2026-09-14)

Account Management

[Phone] Bug fixes for Account Management related services.

Developer Services

[Phone] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Maps related processes in their apps.

Device Connectivity

[Phone, Wear] New developer features for Google and third party app developers to support Device Connectivity related processes in their apps.

System Management

[Auto, PC, Phone, TV, Wear] Bug fixes for System Management & Diagnostics related services.

Wallet

[PC, Phone] Enable real-time cart price adjustments when a user selects or changes their payment method during checkout.

Google Play Store v53.2 (2026-09-14)

[Phone] You can now use the Contribution Hub cluster on the “You” tab to submit ratings and reviews while you track the social impact of your contributions.

Android WebView v154 (2026-09-10)

We changed WebView Finch from Application consistent to Device level consistent.

Improvements to security and privacy and updates for bug fixes.

New developer features for Google & 3rd party app developers to support functionality related to displaying web content in their apps.

Important: Some features may be experimental and available to certain users.

Android AICore

[PC, Phone] Model management enhancements, expanded device compatibility, performance optimizations, and enhancements to diagnostics.

Google Play services v26.35 (2026-09-07)

Account Management

[Phone, Wear] Improvements to Supervision.

[Phone] A new infrastructure within Kids Auth Module to manage and display regulatory compliance notices on Android.

Location & Context

[Phone] This update adds safety status information to shared locations in the location sharing API.

Wallet

[Phone] You can now use NFC to add physical transit card passes and balances to Google Wallet.

[Phone] This update introduces a new “Add a card” success screen with an improved UI.

Google Play Store v53.1 (2026-09-07)

[Phone] You can now find a short description that highlights a key feature in similar apps, in the similar apps section of the app details pages.

[Phone] You can now find on what devices an app is installed when you browse recommendations on the other devices sub-navigation.

[Phone] With a new navigation bar, you can explore more of your interests directly on Play home pages.

Related: How to check if Motion Assist has rolled out to your Android 17 phone

Android System Intelligence B.29 / C.7 (2026-09-03)

[Phone] Bug fixes and maintenance changes.

title: Gemini app starts rolling out big side panel simplification, settings redesign
snippet: The next big update to the Gemini app on Android and iOS is beginning to roll out with a focus on simplifying core navigation. more…
fullText:
The next big update to the Gemini app on Android and iOS is beginning to roll out with a focus on simplifying core navigation.

There are no major changes to the homepage, with the first differences found in the side panel. Search has moved to the top-right corner, while the chat history now offers filters: All, Ready, Needs attention, and In progress.

“Scheduled” is a new item in the list and replaces the “Scheduled actions” page. You get “Suggested” prompts like Create a news digest or Build a study quiz.

“Customize” is the big update today. The “Discover” tab surfaces skills, which are replacing Gems, and third-party connected apps. Notably, skills are activated using the ‘@’ symbol instead of a forward slash like in Gemini Spark. This page feels like a mini-app store for Gemini.

	

Meanwhile, the “Connectors” tab serves as a modernized “Connected Apps” page. Gemini is leaning into that app store parlance with the ability to “Uninstall” from the overflow menu.

Meanwhile, Gemini is getting a much-needed Settings redesign when you tap your profile avatar in the top-right corner or the gear icon. Manage account and Usage limits make up the first grouping, followed by:

Preferences: Notifications, Personal Intelligence, Avatar, Gem manager, Theme, Voice, Media, Device controls, Gemini Notebook

Data & privacy: Import memory, Contact info from your devices, Gemini Apps Activity, Your public links, Privacy Help Hub

Support: Help, Report a problem, About, Updates 

This redesign is not yet widely rolled out and only appearing on one of our Google Accounts. That said, it’s appearing on both Android and iOS.

title: Google says Chromebook updates end in 2034, ‘many’ models move to Googlebook OS
snippet: As Googlebook arrives, Google is offering a bit more information on what Chromebook owners can expect going forward. more…
fullText:
As Googlebook arrives, Google is offering a bit more information on what Chromebook owners can expect going forward.

Google has said that Chromebook updates will continue in the Googlebook era, while some models will also be eligible for upgrades. On a support page, Google provides a bit more detail.

Starting with Chromebook updates, Google says that “Chromebooks you have today will continue to receive updates through their supported lifetime,” with all Enterprise and Education management capabilities remaining in place as well:

We will maintain support for current Chromebook devices running ChromeOS as outlined in our Auto Update policy and the Chromebooks you have today will continue to receive updates through their supported lifetime. Chromebooks remain available for all school and enterprise deployments today.

Your active ChromeOS Enterprise Upgrade and ChromeOS Education Upgrade associated with existing devices will remain and maintain their current management capabilities.

Google adds that similar management tools will be coming to Googlebook, but they’re not available yet. Apparently they’re planned for the second half of 2027. Meanwhile, Google says that “many” existing Chromebook models will be eligible to transition from ChromeOS to Googlebook OS. More details are coming “soon.” A later note specifies that Google is referring to “newer commercial Chromebook models.”

	

Many of our newest Chromebook devices will be eligible to transition over to Googlebook OS. Details on migration paths and device eligibility will be shared soon.

We are working to deliver a comprehensive management experience for Googlebooks which will start rolling out in the second half of 2027.

Notably, Google specifies a year when ChromeOS updates will come to an end in a later note – 2034. Chromebooks with a 10-year update policy that extends past 2034 will be eligible to move to Googlebook OS.

ChromeOS devices will continue to receive regular updates and security patches through mid-2034. For qualifying devices purchased today whose 10-year support lifecycle extends beyond 2034, Google is committed to supporting your transition to Googlebook OS, with many devices offering direct migration paths.

This 2034 date was previously mentioned in a court case as the time when Google would “phase out” ChromeOS.

	

Finally, in regards to apps, Google says that it is “committed” to web developers despite an increased focus on Android apps on Googlebooks.

Googlebook pre-orders are open now, with models shipping in early October.

title: Google details Gems to skills migration, including free access
snippet: As we spotted over the weekend, Gemini is replacing Gems with skills, and Google today fully detailed the migration. more…
fullText:
As we spotted over the weekend, Gemini is replacing Gems with skills, and Google today fully detailed the migration.

The news today is that skills are now available in the Gemini chat experience after debuting in the Spark agent. These reusable instructions for common tasks can be invoked with a / command from the main prompt box instead of having to launch via the Gem manager. This offers a more unified experience in the long run.

Example skills include preparing for presentations, matching writing styles, and getting different perspectives.

Skills will gain feature parity with Gems over the coming weeks. This includes the ability to share skills with others using links, and adding Google Drive files or notebooks for context. 

	

Gemini will automatically migrate Gems to skills, with the new feature available for all free users who don’t have Spark. 

Personal Google Accounts will lose access to Gems starting in November. The migration will happen for Google Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit customers in March 2027, while education users have until June 2027.

Skills start rolling out today to Gemini chat users globally. All other customers can expect access in the coming weeks.

title: Apple releases iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone, here’s what’s new
snippet: Apple has just released iOS 27.0.1, a new iPhone software update with key bug fixes for issues introduced in iOS 27. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Apple has just released iOS 27.0.1, a new iPhone software update with key bug fixes for issues introduced in iOS 27. Here’s what’s new.

iOS 27.0.1 fixes iPhone 18 Pro Face ID issue, plus includes additional bug fixes

iPhone users, Apple has just launched its latest software update. iOS 27.0.1 is now available to install via Settings ⇾ General ⇾ Software Update.

Here’s what Apple’s official release notes say:

This update provides bug fixes for your iPhone, including fixes for the following issues:

iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max may unexpectedly restart when Face ID fails to authenticate

A color artifact may appear on photos captured at 2x under certain lighting conditions at f/1.48 on a small number of iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max devices

Opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously may cause the touchscreen to become unresponsive

As 9to5Mac previously reported, some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max users experienced crashes when Face ID was unable to properly authenticate them. Apple promised a fix was coming this week, and now it has delivered via iOS 27.0.1.

title: Apple releases guide to help families ‘build healthy digital habits’
snippet: Apple has teamed up with the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) to launch a new guide to “help families create healthy digital habits.” The new guide follows Apple’s launch of a range of new child safety features in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
Apple has teamed up with the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) to launch a new guide to “help families create healthy digital habits.” 

The new guide follows Apple’s launch of a range of new child safety features in iOS 27. 

Apple says this new guide is meant to help families balance screen time with sleep, exercise, schoolwork, and socialization. 

The guide includes a six-step breakdown for families, per Apple: 

Start a conversation about screen time, with tips for parents to approach the topic and establish expectations in a way that helps kids feel included in the plan.

Create a Child Account, which enables age-based safeguards and gives parents access to parental controls to manage their child’s experience.

Set safety settings for websites and apps, including Ask to Buy and Ask to Browse, so families can review new apps and websites together.

Make a schedule for device use, using Time Allowances and Schedules to balance time online with sleep, schoolwork, physical activity, and time with family and friends.

Manage communications, with parents deciding who their child can communicate with and Communication Safety, on by default for all users under 18, helping protect kids from viewing or sharing sensitive content.

Continue the conversation as kids grow, with guidance on adjusting the family’s plan over time.

You can find the new guide, “Building Healthy Digital Habits: A Guide for Families,” on Apple’s website.

title: Instagram partner schools can now post content only their students can view
snippet: Meta last year launched a school partnership program for Instagram, in which it promised to prioritize student reports of cyberbullying. The company has now expanded the program to allow schools to post stories and notes that only their own students can view – alongside support for clubs, teams, and more … more…
fullText:
Meta last year launched a school partnership program for Instagram, in which it promised to prioritize student reports of cyberbullying.

The company has now expanded the program to allow schools to post stories and notes that only their own students can view – alongside support for clubs, teams, and more …

Instagram School Partnership Program

Instagram is a platform that doesn’t exactly have the best of track records when it comes to teenage mental health. Even the company’s own internal research showed that Instagram could be harmful to as many as 20% of teenage girls using the apps by increasing anxieties about physical attractiveness and popularity, among other things.

Cyberbullying has been another significant problem for teen users of social networks, and Meta last year launched a program intended to help schools tackle the issue. When schools signed up to its partnership program, Meta promised that reports filed by students and staff would be prioritized.

Reports submitted by school partners that may violate Instagram’s Community Standards will be prioritized for review. Schools will also receive status updates on the reports and notifications as soon as Instagram takes action on the report.

New school features

Meta says it is today adding a number of new features to the program.

Channels. These allow schools to share updates to parents and students. Only school administrators can post messages in channels.

School Stories and notes. Both staff and students can post these, and they will only be visible by verified students at the school. School administrators can remove posts.

Clubs and Teams. Anyone in the school can create clubs and teams to act as a central hub for communicating relevant events and information.

Student directory. Students can access a directory of other students at their school on the platform. This is visible only to other students and teen followers they follow back.

Meta says that the new features are intended for use outside of classroom hours, noting that teen accounts allow parents to block usage during school hours.

Verification of high school students is carried out by UNiDAYS, the same company Apple uses to allow access to educational pricing.

fullText:
Samsung is today officially launching its new Galaxy Tab S12 series with the Tab S12+ and Tab S12 Ultra delivering big displays, powerful specs, and some new software tricks too.

Available starting October 7, the Galaxy Tab S12+ and Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra continue Samsung’s flagship tablet series with some nominal upgrades. While they’re visually almost identical to prior generations, there are some spec bumps, including the new MediaTek Dimensity 9500.

Besides the size, one of the notable differences is that there’s no cellular version of the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra. Samsung has no smaller screen size available this year, with the Galaxy Tab S11 still serving as the 11-inch option.

Both tablets, Samsung says, include a larger vapor chamber for heat dissipation, retain the IP68 dust/water resistance rating of prior models, and ship with One UI 9 (Android 17) out of the box with seven years of OS + security updates. There’s also an S Pen included in the box, with a keyboard cover and other accessories available as add-on purchases.

	

Samsung has new partnerships with productivity apps, too. Adobe Photoshop is pre-installed on the Galaxy Tab S12 series. The app has S Pen optimization and users get four months of free access to the app as well. Notability, a recent arrival on Android, is also pre-loaded and comes with a six-month trial. There are further freebies in Goodnotes, LumaFusion, Notion, and others, as well as a six-month Google AI Pro trial for boosted Gemini capabilities.

Galaxy Tab S12+ starts at $1,199, while Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra starts at $1,399, the latter being a $100 increase over last year. As mentioned, both are available in the US starting October 7.

title: Gemini app replacing Gems with skills in November
snippet: In 2024, Google introduced Gems as “custom versions of Gemini.” The Gemini app will soon replace Gems with “skills.” more…
fullText:
In 2024, Google introduced Gems as “custom versions of Gemini.” The Gemini app will soon replace Gems with “skills.”

Going to the Gems manager today reveals a new notice at the top: “Gems will become skills starting Nov 17, 2026.”

Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating your Gems to skills. You will be able to use your Gems until they migrate.

Google introduced skills with Gemini Spark, and they serve the same purpose as Gems at a high level. Both let you give Gemini custom instructions.

	
	

Gems let you go a step further by setting a default tool, like Create image or Canvas, and adding specific files for context. They can also be shared with other users via links.

That said, skills are more easily invoked with a / in the prompt box, while multiple can be used at the same time. This broader access is better than first having to go to Gems in the side panel and scrolling down for My Gems.

Google’s announcement might have rolled out slightly early as the “Learn more” help article and “Create skills” button do not work yet.

If you’re a Google AI Pro or AI Ultra subscriber, you can make skills by switching to the Gemini Spark tab. Typing a slash in the Chat box will let you use skills in the main conversational experience.

title: Amazon introduces Kindle Click, a $35 remote for turning pages
snippet: The compact Bluetooth remote is designed to let readers turn pages without touching their Kindle.
fullText:
Alongside a redesigned Kindle lineup that features slimmer designs, zero bezels, and a lighter feel, Amazon announced a range of new accessories on Thursday. And one of them, a $34.99 remote called the Kindle Click, caught our eye.

The Kindle Click is a compact Bluetooth remote designed to let readers turn pages without touching their Kindle. The idea is simple, but it could solve a surprisingly common annoyance for e-reader owners who have to reach over and tap the screen every time they want to move to the next page.

The small remote is designed for situations where touching the Kindle isn’t convenient. Amazon specifically positions it for reading under the covers, on a treadmill, or with a Kindle resting on a tray table during a flight. Instead of reaching for the e-reader, readers can simply press a button on the remote to turn the page.

The new accessory is compatible with all new Kindle devices, as well as Kindle models released in 2024 and later.

For years, Kindle owners have largely relied on third-party accessories, many of which use a clip-on mechanism that physically touches the display rather than communicating directly with the Kindle. 

The Kindle Click puts Amazon into a category that competitors have already started exploring. Rakuten Kobo, for instance, launched its $29.99 Kobo Remote last year. There’s also the BOOX Tappy, a $29.99 wireless page turner designed for BOOX ePaper devices.

While Amazon’s Kindle Click is priced higher than these competing accessories, the company is likely betting that Kindle owners will pay for an official accessory designed specifically for the lineup. This new Kindle lineup, one of the most significant physical redesigns in years, has a display that Amazon says is 30% faster at page turns than the previous generation.

Amazon also announced other accessories as part of the new Kindle family, including a magnetic cover with physical page-turn buttons and a charging dock stand for the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition and Colorsoft Signature Edition.

title: I Tested the Three Big Voice Assistants to See Who’s Best at Predicting Weather
snippet: Pitting Gemini, Alexa Plus and Siri AI against each other revealed how well these assistants can interpret local weather.
fullText:
Ever wonder which voice assistant knows your weather the best? For the past couple of months, I’ve been testing out the big three — Amazon’s Alexa Plus, Google Gemini for Home (which is busy replacing Google Assistant) and Apple’s Siri AI — to see who gets the weather right most often. They all pull their weather data from the internet, but their sources and algorithms lead to drastically different results.

Read more: Best Smart Speakers for 2026

My high desert city makes an excellent review location for weather reports, from the federal cuts to weather stations and forecast funding to our many microclimates coexisting under the Cascade Mountains. It’s the perfect spot for voice assistants to test their mettle, plus the online sources they draw their weather data from, allowing us to see which is accurate in tough conditions.

			

More from CNET

If you like asking your voice assistant about today’s weather as you prep for work, school or even camping plans, here are my real-world results, and which assistant ultimately proved best.

Alexa Plus: The chatty, overconfident relative

Alexa’s weather responses are chatty and often randomized with extra info.

Wow, Alexa loves to chat. While the AI voice assistant has several personalities to pick from, mine is on the standard setting but frequently enjoys talking things out.

Not only does Alexa typically have the longest weather reports, but it also provides the most detail, for better and worse. Alexa Plus is the voice assistant to get extra tidbits about the wind level, snow advisories, air quality levels, chances of rain in the afternoon and other data, some more useful than others. The voice assistant also frequently makes asides, like explaining, “It’s 55 out but feels more like 65” due to the sun and lack of wind or other weather elements.

Exact weather predictions were generally accurate, but the assistant occasionally slipped up, such as predicting rain when none materialized. Alexa often overestimated the highs and lows in my area by a few degrees, too.

Amazon must have Alexa equipped with some sort of randomizer because none of this info is guaranteed, and the greetings and phrasing tend to change regularly. It’s fun, but it’s a little wild and not always accurate. A few times, Alexa tried to tell me my desert climate was at “99% humidity,” possibly because some online discussion about relative humidity got mixed in.

If you like extra info and don’t mind things being random, Alexa Plus may be your best pick, although the accuracy of its weather report isn’t always top-notch. Keep in mind, Alexa Plus is free with an Amazon Prime subscription but will otherwise cost around $20 per month. Also, while I tested the standard version of Alexa Plus, choosing different personalities or asking it to be more terse can help cut down on the info you get, so Alexa has plenty of customization options available here.

Read more: The Ultimate Guide to the Best Amazon Alexa Voice Commands

Gemini for Home: The no-nonsense reporter

Gemini tend to prefer accuracy overall.

Interestingly, Gemini on my Nest Hub narrowed results down to my exact neighborhood instead of the city as a whole. I don’t know how much this affected weather predictions, but Gemini proved the most accurate out of the voice assistants. Its highs and lows were typically accurate within a degree or two, and it didn’t overestimate like Alexa did. (If anything, it tended to undershoot the highs.)

While a quick “Hey Google” may yield the best weather reports, the voice assistant doesn’t provide much more info. Sometimes Gemini added info about overcast skies or rain, but nothing to the extent of Alexa.

If short and sweet is your preference, this is the most reliable option. I also like Gemini’s visuals best, with the forecast divided into hours so you can easily see when temperatures reach their height or when clouds are likely to move in.

Siri: The hesitant moderate

The information Siri proved was brief compared to the other voice assistants.

While not quite as formal as Gemini, Siri is likewise terse on weather reports and didn’t volunteer any extra info, like cloudy skies or rain, unless specifically asked in follow-up questions.

As for accuracy, Siri’s estimates were typically somewhere between Alexa’s slightly overblown expectations and Gemini’s more conservative approach, making it the moderate of the bunch.

That makes Siri a reasonable option for weather predictions, except I noticed what seemed like an odd bug where Apple’s voice assistant would suddenly forecast a high about five degrees higher than the other options and way off the mark. Sometimes it would do the same with lows, citing a temperature five degrees lower than what they actually reached.

I’m not sure why this discrepancy crept in, but it made Siri less reliable over time during my daily tests.

Bottom line

Alexa is more advanced than ever, especially with third-party connections.Ty Pendlebury/CNET

If you have an eye on accuracy and reliable weather reports when heading out in the morning, I recommend Gemini’s brief but good weather summaries. If you can get them on a smart display, like a Nest Hub, it also offers my favorite accompanying graphics.

Alexa Plus, however, wins for the sheer amount of information it provides and its chatty nature. You may never be sure what your weather report will include, but it’s likely to have a bit of everything, and you can ask Alexa to tone it down if need be.

Siri, meanwhile, had some issues suddenly overshooting or undershooting the mark and didn’t provide any helpful details, making it the least effective at handling your weather needs.

Who gives the most accurate current temperature readings?

Google has focus on Gemini and its own home speakers thus far.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Along with predictions, I also tested out voice assistant abilities to give current temperature readings. Since I have smart thermostats and plenty of portable air quality monitors from my testing, this was easy to double-check and see how they performed.

The voice assistants typically stayed within a couple of degrees of the temperature outside my house. In most cases, they were a degree or two lower, but nothing problematic.

The exception is Siri, where that odd bug estimating the temperature about five degrees higher than it was crept in once more. I couldn’t figure out what caused that bug, but it did make Siri occasionally wrong in contrast to the other voice assistants.

A final tip now that you have the lowdown on the weather: You can sync up weather reports, traffic reports, news and other tidbits in a single morning routine so voice assistants provide you with all this information at once, usually with a phrase like “Good morning.” It can be a timesaver — see my guide for more information.

fullText:
HP is announcing a new laptop that’s squarely aimed at Apple’s MacBook Neo. The 2026 HP OmniBook 5 14 starts at $699.99 with an Intel Core 5 315 “Wildcat Lake” processor, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. Much of that sounds pretty familiar, being in lockstep with both Apple’s Neo and its recent competition from Dell, Asus, and Acer — the HP even offers a similar four color options in silver, pink, blue, and green. But one thing that separates the OmniBook is its inclusion of an OLED display on all configs.

The OmniBook 5 14 can be configured much higher, with up to a Core 7 350 chip, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, but all models include a 1080p webcam, dual speakers, HDMI, 3.5mm audio jack, and just two 10Gbps USB-C ports. And while the inclusion of OLED across the range is a major draw to the new OmniBook, the base config only has a passable 1920 x 1200 resolution and 300 nits of max brightness on its non-touch panel. A touchscreen version will be available when the OmniBook 5 launches in October, but a version with a 2560 x 1600 resolution OLED and 400 nits of brightness isn’t coming until March 2027.

1/8The OmniBook 5 14. Image: HP

While the OmniBook 5 14 doesn’t seem poised to best the MacBook Neo in raw processing power (based on our other reviews of Wildcat Lake laptops) or screen brightness, it’s quite thin, light, and colorful. HP even gave it the nicer, sleeker lid logo usually reserved for pricier models. It starts at just 2.56 pounds, and it’s as thin as 0.46 inches / 11.7mm. That’s slightly lighter and thinner than a Neo. And I’d expect its Wildcat Lake chips to offer some good-to-great battery life. But we’ll have to see how it delivers in actual testing.

Alongside the OmniBook 5 14, HP is also announcing a new ProBook 4 G2iS business laptop that it claims at 0.47 inches / 12mm is its “thinnest business notebook.” It’ll also start with Intel Wildcat Lake chips, 8GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD when it launches in December, but there’s no price yet.

1/3The HP ProBook 4 G2iS. Image: HP

title: Apple faces renewed scrutiny over removal of ICEBlock from the App Store
snippet: CNN reports that Rep. Jamie Raskin sent a letter to Apple this week challenging the company’s explanation for removing ICEBlock from the App Store last year. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
CNN reports that Rep. Jamie Raskin sent a letter to Apple this week challenging the company’s explanation for removing ICEBlock from the App Store last year. Here are the details.

ICEBlock removal once again under scrutiny

According to CNN, Apple sent a letter to Rep. Jamie Raskin last July explaining its decision to remove ICEBlock and similar apps from the App Store, and Raskin has now responded with new questions about the company’s justification.

For context, ICEBlock was one of the most prominent apps that allowed users to report and track ICE activity in their area. The app rapidly rose in popularity during the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, growing from around 20,000 users to roughly one million within weeks.

As its popularity skyrocketed, ICEBlock became the target of the US government, with then-Attorney General Pam Bondi publicly calling for Apple to remove the app and warning its developer that he could face prosecution.

Following pressure from the DOJ, Apple removed it and several similar apps from the App Store, citing concerns over the safety of federal agents. The move came shortly after a gunman opened fire on an ICE facility in Dallas, ultimately killing two detainees in an attack that federal authorities described as targeted violence against ICE.

This, in turn, prompted Raskin to investigate whether the Trump administration had pressured Apple and Google into removing ICE-tracking apps, and what impact those removals may have had on constitutionally protected speech.

As part of that investigation, CNN reports that Apple sent Raskin a letter last July explaining why it removed ICEBlock and similar apps from the App Store.

From CNN:

Apple says its decision to remove ICEBlock and similar platforms from the app store last year was prompted by concerns — including those raised by the Trump administration — about agent safety following a fatal shooting that left two detainees dead at a Dallas Immigration and Customs Enforcement office.

Apple’s explanation came in a July letter to Rep. Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat and ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, who earlier this year launched an investigation into the Justice Department’s role in the removal of the apps from Apple’s and Google’s app stores and the impact on constitutionally protected speech. The letter has not previously been reported.

CNN says that Apple’s letter to Raskin also mentioned that the company approved ICEBlock in April 2025, after developer Joshua Aaron addressed what Apple referred to as “certain user privacy concerns.”

Apple also reportedly said it continued to monitor news coverage and criticism of the app in the months that followed, ultimately deciding to remove ICEBlock and similar apps after concluding they violated its App Store guidelines by providing “precise location information about ICE officers,” which could potentially be used for targeted attacks.

Apple also cited concerns raised by Bondi after the Dallas shooting, as well as comments from FBI Director Kash Patel that the shooter had searched for apps that tracked ICE agents’ locations.

According to Apple, those concerns, together with what it described as a broader increase in ICE activity and threats against agents, prompted the company to conduct a new review of ICEBlock.

Raskin pushes back

According to CNN, Raskin sent a letter to Apple this week further questioning the company’s justification for removing ICEBlock and similar apps from the App Store.

	

From CNN:

Raskin said the move suggests that Apple may be “working with the government to violate its customers’ First Amendment rights to record and report on the activities of their own government” in a response letter sent Monday to Apple’s senior director of government affairs, Timothy Powderly.

CNN also notes that Raskin disputed Apple’s reliance on the Dallas shooting, arguing that the gunman did not need an ICE-tracking app to locate a fixed government facility and reportedly found the address using “an app that comes standard on Apple devices.”

He also pointed to other navigation apps that remain available on the App Store despite providing real-time information about law enforcement locations, and asked Apple to conduct a new independent review of the removals and provide a full list of apps it removed in response to concerns raised by the DOJ.

title: Report: Meta’s Muse crosses 5 million downloads amid massive advertising push
snippet: Meta’s streak at the top of the App Store continues in the US and Canada, as its AI assistant Muse is now past 5 million downloads, according to Sensor Tower. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Meta’s streak at the top of the App Store continues in the US and Canada, as its AI assistant Muse is now past 5 million downloads, according to Sensor Tower. Here are the details.

Muse continues its 12-day streak at the top of the US App Store

Three weeks ago, Meta launched Muse in the US. Soon after, it overtook ChatGPT as the top free app in the US App Store

Today, according to a projection by Sensor Tower Senior Insights Analyst Kara Lee, Muse crossed 5 million downloads. That means it reached the milestone considerably faster than ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude, which the market intelligence firm says took 56, 103, and 492 days, respectively.

Source: Sensor Tower

Muse is Meta’s agentic AI assistant, capable of browsing the web and carrying out tasks on a user’s behalf, including sending emails, shopping, filling out forms, and booking travel.

Sensor Tower adds that Claude and Grok were iOS-exclusive in their first 5 days. Meta’s Muse app, by contrast, is available on iOS and Android, but only in the US and Canada.

Here’s Sensor Tower with more context on how Muse’s 5 million-download milestone compares to other major app launches:

According to Sensor Tower estimates, only 23 apps have reached over 5mn US downloads within 22 days of launch. ~85% of these apps are mobile gaming apps, including Fortnite, Pokemon GO, Candy Crush, and more. There were only 3 apps within that list that are not gaming apps, including Disney+, HBO Max, and Threads, which received ~20mn, 18mn, and 14mn downloads during that time, respectively.

	

The report adds that while Meta’s Muse app appears to have attracted significant public interest, Meta’s own advertising push has likely played a role in its rapid adoption.

Sensor Tower says “Meta began to ramp advertising spend for Muse on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, as downloads spiked 73% DoD,” and adds:

According to Sensor Tower data, Muse has received the largest share of Meta’s house ads, accounting for up to 50% of daily house impressions over the past two weeks (9/14-927), as Facebook and WhatsApp ceded share of impressions during the same period.

Sensor Tower also says Muse ranked among the top 15 brands by advertising impressions in the US during the week of September 21 through September 27.

title: Galaxy S27 Ultra’s missing camera shown in leaks is its 3x zoom
snippet: Previous Galaxy S27 Ultra leaks have directed attention to the new camera island, but don’t overlook the missing camera lens left behind with the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Apparently, that camera is the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra’s 10MP 3x zoom. more…
fullText:
Previous Galaxy S27 Ultra leaks have directed attention to the new camera island, but don’t overlook the missing camera lens left behind with the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Apparently, that camera is the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra’s 10MP 3x zoom.

We’ve seen a selection of leaks with details galore, including privacy displays, battery upgrades, and more. Any render that’s come out has shown off an entirely new camera island design, and it’s become the focus of the new phone. Love it or hate it, it’s there and almost square.

According to another leak via @UniverseIce on Twitter/X, the Galaxy S27 Ultra won’t have a 3x optical zoom lens with a 10MP sensor. Instead, the phone will have a wide 1x lens setup and a 5x optical zoom unit – 50MP, if left unchanged as suggested.

It is now confirmed that the Galaxy S27 Ultra will no longer have a 3× telephoto camera.

This means its rear camera system will jump directly from the 1× main camera to the 5× telephoto camera.

The main camera uses the ISOCELL HP6, essentially a Galaxy-customized version of the… https://t.co/qYGcdX93oy

— Ice Universe (@UniverseIce) September 29, 2026

The latest renders clearly show a missing lens if you compare the phone to last year’s model. The Galaxy S26 Ultra had a 3x and 5x optical zoom camera, totaling four sensors across the back of the phone. Now, sitting in a section of much larger real estate, the new camera array appears to have only three cameras.

	

A render posted by @OnLeaks labels portions of the new panel. Where previous renders showed another lens underneath the flash LED, this new render places the LED at the bottom, topped by additional sensors, a microphone, and what may now be the 5x zoom lens.

As is the case with nearly every Galaxy S series leak, these are to be taken with a grain of salt. Renders have come and gone, but we won’t know the final details until Samsung launches the device sometime in early 2027.

fullText:
Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is a weekly 9to5Mac series where we showcase the latest apps in the indie app world. If you’re a developer and would like your app featured, get in contact.

iOS 27 debuted to the public almost two weeks ago, with the flagship feature being Siri AI. While Siri AI was revolutionary compared to what existed prior, it still has some shortcomings. QuillCue aims to close one of the gaps with Siri AI by providing a custom keyboard that lets you save prompts for later.

Highlights

QuillCue is a rather great concept. Using custom keyboards on iOS, it allows you to insert fully prewritten prompts into Siri AI. Just swipe down from the top of your screen, switch over to the custom keyboard, select your prompt, and press enter.

It saves a lot of time if you have Siri questions you end up asking regularly, but don’t want to always type the same thing over and over again. One of the default prompts is finding nearby coffee shops that allow laptops for remote work. Since this is dependent on location, it’s always great to fetch new results that you might’ve not known about. 

Of course, you can pre-write any prompt that Siri AI can handle. QuillCue just saves you the hassle of having to respeak or retype it every single time, making Siri AI a lot easier to use.

If you end up writing a rather lengthy prompt full of different steps, QuillCue can save you a lot of time – since Siri AI doesn’t currently have a concept of ‘skills’ or learning from your usage. The possibilities are really endless. The app also offers folders for sorting your different prompts.

Lastly, it also offers the ability to import and export prompt libraries, so if you’d like to share prompts with friends or transfer them between devices, you can do so easily.

Download the app

QuillCue is available for free on the App Store, with no ads or in app purchases. You can follow the developer Parker Ortolani on X for updates. 

It requires an iPhone running iOS 27.0 or later, and is currently limited to users in the United States.

title: Feature Request: One change for the most important use of Notify Me
snippet: A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs. This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me … more…
fullText:
A key new feature in macOS 27 is Safari’s Notify Me function. This has the Apple Intelligence automatically monitor a web page for updates and send a notification when it occurs.

This feature can be useful in a wide variety of ways, with price drops being one of the most obvious. Unfortunately, a limitation means that it doesn’t yet support what I would consider the most important use case for Notify Me …

Given that computers were supposed to automate boring tasks so that humans didn’t have to do them, it’s somewhat disappointing just how frequently we find ourselves doing tedious and repetitive tasks that somehow can’t yet be easily automated. AI is changing this, and Apple’s Notify Me feature in Safari is a good example.

For example, if I’m waiting for a product to come back into stock in order to place an order, or delaying my purchase until the price drops to a more reasonable level, Safari can now monitor a web page and let me know when it’s time to buy.

But the single most tedious manual refreshing of websites I do on a regular basis is waiting for tickets to go on sale. There are some events that sell out within minutes of ticket sales opening, and as they frequently don’t happen exactly at the promised time, I often find myself visiting a website a few minutes before sales are supposed to begin and then repeatedly refreshing the page. 

In some cases, the sales window can open 20 or 30 minutes later than promised, so this process can grow extremely time-consuming and tedious. This is a perfect use case for the Notify Me feature.

Unfortunately, it can’t be used for this because the highest frequency check I can set is hourly. By the time Safari notifies me, there’s a high chance that all tickets would be sold out, or at least the ones for the seats that I really wanted.

I’d like one simple change: the ability to set the check frequency to every minute or even every 15 seconds.

I appreciate that people doing this for an extended period could effectively amount to a denial of service attack on a website, so Apple would have to impose limits on its use. A simple one would be to allow high-frequency checks to run for a maximum period of 30 minutes. Given that we wouldn’t typically need to check the same website very often, the company could even have a reset time of a month before we can use the feature again on the same website.

Is there something you’d like to see? Please take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments.

title: Google Antigravity Googlebook app hits the Play Store
snippet: Ahead of the Googlebook launch, Google Antigravity is now available in the Play Store. more…
fullText:
Ahead of the Googlebook launch, Google Antigravity is now available in the Play Store.

Antigravity is Google’s agent-first development platform, with version 2.0 released at I/O 2026 in May. It serves as a “dedicated mission control to work alongside, steer, and customize agents that operate autonomously in the background.”

After creating macOS, Windows, and Linux versions, Antigravity is now available on Android with a native interface. It interacts with the Linux environment available on the new laptops. You can “Create and deploy apps right on your Googlebook.”

The package name is com.google.android.apps.antigravity, and the app is currently on version 2026.09.23.988012583.

	

That said, it’s currently only available on Googlebook OS. The interface might work on tablets and foldables, but it’s unclear if Google designed it for smaller phone screens. 

The interface looks similar to the other desktop versions, but it remains to be seen whether it will retain feature parity given how quickly the other apps are updated with major features on a weekly basis.

Antigravity on Googlebooks is part of Google’s push to make the new platform suitable for developers. You can also just install the Linux version of Antigravity on Googlebooks, along with Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex. Additionally, Google advertised the ability to install the Antigravity CLI via the Googlebook terminal.

title: iOS 27.2 adds new Messages feature that’s already a favorite
snippet: iOS 27.2 is coming soon with several new features for iPhone users, including a Messages addition that was previously in the iOS 27 beta but later got pulled: Suggestions. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 is coming soon with several new features for iPhone users, including a Messages addition that was previously in the iOS 27 beta but later got pulled: Suggestions.

Messages ‘Suggestions’ return in iOS 27.2 after being pulled from iOS 27 beta

Throughout the iOS 27 beta this summer, one of my favorite AI features was a Messages addition that didn’t feel like AI at all: Suggestions.

Here’s what they do, per Apple:

Messages offers one-tap suggestions based on the context of users’ conversations, making it easier than ever to get things done, such as creating a reminder or a note. For example, if someone asks for photos, Messages can also help users find the right ones, recognizing keywords, locations, and people in their library to find the best options.

Suggestions appear as small, convenient action buttons beneath messages they’re relevant to.

As seen in the image below, if someone asks you to do something, you might see a suggestion to add to Reminders or Notes. Or if an event is mentioned, suggestions lets you easily add it to your calendar.

Suggestions worked well for me in the iOS 27 beta, but shortly before the fall public launch, Apple delayed the feature into a “future software update.”

Now in the iOS 27.2 beta, suggestions are back. And one way they’ve changed might explain why they were pulled in the first place.

As I mentioned, suggestions performed as expected for me during the summer. But if I had one complaint, it was that they sometimes appeared when a message’s context didn’t merit them. At times I saw suggestions to add things to Notes, Reminders, or Calendar when there wasn’t a clear justification for these recommendations.

But so far at least, in my testing of iOS 27.2 there are fewer suggestions appearing in my Messages conversations. When I see them, it’s always obvious why they’re being suggested.

Here’s hoping the feature makes the shipping version of iOS 27.2 in just a few weeks.

How have suggestions been working for you in iOS 27.2? Let us know in the comments.

title: Craig Federighi on how Apple helps developers make the most of the iPhone Duo [Video]
snippet: Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with the hinge mechanism in the iPhone Duo. He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device … more…
fullText:
Apple software chief Craig Federighi said in an interview that he is excited to see what developers will do with the hinge mechanism in the iPhone Duo.

He said an API lets developers read the angle of the hinge with an accuracy of around five degrees, and the ability to read what Apple describes as the “pose” of the device …

Apple itself uses the hinge angle in a number of ways in software, including a feature that became an instant hit: the way the outer screen defocuses into a preview of the inner one as you open the phone. He told Donald Decodes that the feature is subtle but magical.

The goal was not a fancy animation you’d think about, but something you’d perceive automatically: the screen becomes translucent, a window to what’s below. Fundamental to the device is continuity between your experience when it’s closed and what you find when you open it. Seeing through the screen above to what’s about to be revealed below eases that journey in the most natural way. We’re really delighted with how it came out. It’s subtle but magical.

Federighi says he is confident that developers will do creative and exciting things with the hinge information exposed, just as they have with other iPhone data made available to them.

For most developers […] we’re focused on communicating the pose of the device: are you in book pose, on-table pose, tent pose? Developers don’t have to work with how many degrees open it is. By communicating the pose, the frameworks can react automatically and deliver a consistent experience across apps. But for creative experiences, like our own animation, developers can get closer to the raw information […]

We have a long history of exposing gyroscope and accelerometer data to developers, and they’ve made really interesting use of it over time. One of the ways this device expresses itself is through its poses and the hinge, and we’re excited to see what developers do with it.

He said Apple has also worked hard to make it easier for developers to create apps that take full advantage of the iPhone Duo’s capabilities.

We’ve built our platform on high-level frameworks like UIKit and SwiftUI that abstract away many of the harder layout problems, so apps often inherit new behaviors automatically. Over time we’ve added more high-level constructs that adapt automatically, which makes this transition nearly automatic for many developers.

He added that Apple also supports agentic coding tools to enable developers to adapt existing apps almost completely automatically. You can watch the interview below.

title: Google Health 5.09 rolling out: Cardio Load from third-party workouts, more
snippet: Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch. more…
fullText:
Following yesterday’s announcement, Google Health 5.09 is rolling out with support for the new Health Guardian features on the Pixel Watch.

With version 5.09 for Android, Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users can set up blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. The first monthly Health Guardian summary will appear at the beginning of October, while you can also find information in the Health tab afterwards:

Blood pressure trends, that allow you to track blood pressure patterns before they can put strain on your heart, will be available in the Heart section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 5 or more consecutive days in September.

Insulin resistance trends will be available in the Metabolic section of the Health tab if you’ve worn your watch for 7 or more days and nights in September.

Sleep breathing quality metrics, so you can learn how your sleep breathing patterns can affect your daily energy, will be available in the Sleep tab and Respiratory section of the Health tab. You’ll be able to see both daily and monthly trends.

There are also three other sets of improvements with Google Health 5.09 on Android and iOS:

	

Cardio Load for Workouts Started in Other Apps

	

Since launch, Google Health has allowed you to connect your favorite apps and devices to the Google Health experience. Now, the workouts you track in other apps and devices and sync to Google Health can count toward your Cardio Load, as long as the other app or device has tracked your heart rate data during that workout. This means workouts you track on other wearables like a Garmin or Apple Watch and sync to Google Health will earn Cardio Load.

Nutrition Improvements

When creating a custom food, you can now toggle food serving units and meal time more easily.

We’ve resolved an issue with custom food creation on iOS and fixed a bug where deleted items could still appear in your custom food list.

Activity and Fitness Updates

You now have more options for how you log your completed activities on the Fitness tab. Tap the “Log activity” button to see them all.

We’ve fixed an issue where some historical step streaks were missing. We are now restoring this data, and your missing streaks will reappear soon.”

title: EVgo’s Next-Gen 750kW EV Charging System Is Capable of 10-Minute Recharge
snippet: The company estimates its fastest-charging tech yet is coming next year, but it’ll be a while before cars can hit its top speed.
fullText:
This week, electric vehicle fast-charging developer and network operator EVgo announced its new 750-kilowatt EV charging system to the world. With speeds nearly double that of the current fastest public chargers in the US and Europe, compatible next-gen EVs could recharge in as little as 10 minutes. The tech is expected to be fully revealed in 2027.

EVgo isn’t alone in pushing the charging envelope. Earlier this year, ChargePoint launched its new Express Solo DC fast-charging station, capable of delivering 600 kW of power. Meanwhile, Chinese automakers, like BYD, as well as European automakers and charging tech companies, are prototyping and deploying liquid-cooled Megawatt Piles, which are said to recharge compatible EVs in five minutes or less. Beyond making pit stops more convenient, future superspeed charging tech also has potential for full-electric heavy trucks and electric air mobility.

The new 750 kW stations

The new 750 kW charging system will use the North American Charging Standard, pioneered by Tesla, which has been adopted by most upcoming North American EVs. EVgo says the move is part of a strategy to double the effective reach of its network by welcoming NACS drivers and not requiring them to have an adapter. (Of course, that still means the thousands of EVs on the road with a CCS plug will have to adapt.) 

			

More from CNET

The stated 750 kW max is the station’s theoretical top speed for future EVs capable of ingesting that much power. On average, the fastest-charging EVs on the road today can only accept up to 350 kW, with actual charging speed determined by battery condition, temperature and state of charge. Many more are only capable of around 150 kW.

Additionally, most EVs ramp up to their sweet-spot speed and then slow down the charging as they approach full capacity to protect the battery, so they’ll still be limited to their specific max speed and charging curve. It may be a while before cars capable of a 10-minute charge hit the road.

EVgo says that it is one of the only American charging networks to design its own chargers.EVgo

More robust, more reliable

EVgo also says the new stations will feature an updated cable design that’s easier to maneuver and a touchless payment interface. Dynamic power sharing is built into the spec, meaning the available charge rate is distributed between connected EVs, so there’s no more worrying about that driver in the older 50 kW EV hogging the fast plug. The new chargers will also have more robust hardware and software, which should improve reliability. There are few things more nerve-racking for a new EV driver than pulling up to a broken station, so I’m hoping EVgo pays particular attention to this promise.

Currently, EVgo operates more than 1,200 fast charging locations across the US. The network operator and charging tech company is designing and testing the next-generation charging system at its lab in El Segundo, California, with codevelopment support from partner Delta Electronics. The final charger design is expected to be unveiled in 2027 as EVgo begins to deploy the new architecture.

title: Gotta Go Fast and Hunt Demons This October in These Free PlayStation Plus Games
snippet: Conquering monsters in Hunt: Showdown 1896 is a fitting way to celebrate the Halloween season.
fullText:
October is a month filled with longer nights, spooky ghost stories and plenty of ghouls and monsters. If you subscribe to any PlayStation Plus plan, you can enjoy those things from the comfort of your cozy home by playing Hunt: Showdown 1896 starting on Oct. 6.

PlayStation Plus, which is Sony’s version of Xbox Game Pass, offers a large, constantly expanding library of games. Subscribers can choose from the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers, each with unique perks and benefits. Starting at $11 a month, the plans give subscribers access to monthly games and rewards, and each month, all subscribers can access a handful of games at no additional charge.

		

			

Here are all the games PlayStation Plus subscribers can play from Oct. 6 until Nov. 2.

Hunt: Showdown 1896

Danger lurks around every corner in this player-versus-player extraction shooter set in an alternate 19th century. You can play as a bounty hunter with up to two others searching for one of six demons across four open-world maps, or you can fight against other players for loot. No matter what, you should have a wicked good time.

F1 25

The officially licensed video game of the 2025 FIA Formula One Championship is coming to PlayStation Plus. Two new teams joined the F1 franchise in this series installment: Audi and Cadillac, the first major US car manufacturer in F1. You’ll also experience lighter, smaller cars in this installment, which presents all-new driving mechanics you’ll have to learn. Do you have what it takes to beat Lando Norris to the Drivers’ Championship? 

Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2

The square Earth is in pieces… again! Giant ants, spiders, bees and other gargantuan enemies are wreaking havoc, and it’s up to you and your team to stop them. You’ll construct a team that complements your play style, build your arsenal and defend the planet. Whether you’re on a round or square planet, you’ll defend it from all threats.

For more on PlayStation Plus, here’s what to know about the gaming service. You can also check out the latest and upcoming games on Xbox Game Pass.

title: iOS 27.2: Three new features coming soon to your iPhone
snippet: iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.0.1 just launched yesterday, but Apple is already well on its way to preparing iOS 27.2 as a forthcoming iPhone update (with 27.1 likely iPhone Duo-only). Here are three new features coming with iOS 27.2.

#1: Dual Capture for Group FaceTime

FaceTime got one of its biggest upgrades in years with iOS 27. 

On compatible iPhone models, Dual Capture lets you display both your front and rear camera views at the same time. Just tap the ‘Flip’ button and the back camera will go live while the front camera remains active.

And in iOS 27.2, the feature gets even better by adding support for Group FaceTime calls.

iOS 27 currently only lets you use Dual Capture in one-on-one calls, but with iOS 27.2 it will be available for Group FaceTime too.

#2: Apple Podcasts overhauls ‘Up Next’ queue

Apple Podcasts gets a key change in iOS 27.2 that I’m already a big fan of in the beta.

The previous ‘Up Next’ queue at the top of the app’s Home tab is being split into two new sections:

New Episodes replaces Up Next, and contains the latest releases for shows you follow

Continue Playing is brand new, located directly below New Episodes as a hub for all in-progress shows

I’ve criticized the Up Next feature before for being cluttered and confusing, so I’m very excited to see this change. In my early testing, I think it’s a huge improvement that helps users better keep track of everything they’re listening to.

#3: Apple TV app supports user profiles

Apple’s TV app is about to support user profiles on iPhone, bringing the feature over from tvOS to iOS for the first time.

When you first launch the TV app in iOS 27.2, you’ll see a new profile selection screen. You can easily disable it from ever showing up again. But if your child ever watches videos on your iPhone, you might be very glad about this new feature.

With profiles, the Apple TV app can change which content it displays and recommends based on the selected viewer. And importantly, when a child’s profile is active, they’ll only see age-appropriate series and movies from Apple. So not only does your own personal viewing queue stay uncluttered, but you also ensure your child doesn’t see something they shouldn’t.

fullText:
Apple has new beta firmware rolling out now for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and select other models. Here are the details.

Apple releases new AirPods beta firmware for select models

If your AirPods have an H2 chip, there’s new beta firmware rolling out now for early testing.

Apple’s latest AirPods beta firmware has build number 9B5042a.

For reference, the current public version of AirPods firmware across AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, and more is 9A348. And the just-launched AirPods 5 use 9A350.

The new firmware is now available for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods 5, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

It’s unknown what changes the latest firmware introduces. Apple might be laying the groundwork for new features coming in iOS 27.1 or 27.2. Or the update might focus primarily on bug fixes and performance improvements.

If you’re interested in testing out the AirPods firmware before it launches to all users, you can opt into beta updates from the AirPods settings screen on your iPhone.

There’s no way to manually trigger a firmware update, but Apple has instructions here for ensuring the automatic update happens quickly.

Make sure that your iPhone, iPad, or Mac is updated to the latest version of iOS, iPadOS, or macOS, and that Bluetooth is on.

Make sure that your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Connect your iPhone, iPad, or Mac to Wi-Fi.

Connect your charging case to power.

Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to update.

Open the lid of the charging case to reconnect your AirPods to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.

Check the firmware version again.

title: Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag 3 works with iPhones, but not Android Find Hub
snippet: Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users. more…
fullText:
Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users.

In a press release today, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a “smaller, lighter” tracker. Specifically, it’s 35% smaller and 33% lighter. It shrinks down by ditching the built-in mounting loop, instead relying on add-on cases and accessories to connect to other objects. Samsung says the tracker has 550 days of battery life in typical use and up to 790 in “Power Saving Mode,” while also supporting both Bluetooth 6.0 with channel sounding and UWB for precise finding.

Galaxy SmartTag 3 integrates with the Galaxy Find Network which is available on Galaxy smartphones and usable through the SmartThings Find app. Samsung touts over 900 million Galaxy devices building out the network.

New this time around, too, is support for tracking down a SmartTag 3 via iPhone. Samsung’s app on iPhone supports finding the tracker, though it doesn’t contribute to the network. Still rather handy for families with multiple types of devices.

	

While iPhone support has been added, Samsung’s new tracker still doesn’t integrate with the wider Android Find Hub network which works across all Android devices rather than only Galaxy.

Other new features include:

Place Notification… adds a proactive layer, letting users define an area and receive an alert when a tagged item moves in or out of it.

Location History lets users review where their tag has been

Movement Detection Alert can notify them when movement is detected so they can stay informed without actively checking.

NFC-powered Lost Mode, which can display registered contact information or a short message when a lost tag is scanned with a compatible mobile device.

SmartThings IoT Control, which allows users to trigger preset routines for compatible connected devices using the tag button.

Left Behind Alert, which can notify users when their mobile device loses connection with a tagged belonging.

The Galaxy SmartTag 3 will be available on October 7, the same date as Samsung’s new Galaxy Tab S12 series.
