title: Fake iPhone Duo preorder page can steal crypto wallet data and more
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now. The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now.

The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … 

Security researchers at Malwarebytes say the page uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which works with some older unpatched iPhones. You don’t have to do anything, just visiting the page is enough for the attack to launch.

Behind its Apple-style design and $500 voucher, the page uses the leaked DarkSword exploit chain to try to break into vulnerable iPhones. If it succeeds, a separate payload attempts to steal saved credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and notes. You don’t have to fill in the form, tap a download, or approve anything. Opening the page is enough to start the attempt.

If it succeeds, then it captures your device identifier information and status and attempts to send a list of installed apps and the contents of your Apple Notes. Having done this, it turns its attention to crypto wallets.

The code looks for cryptocurrency wallets, including MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Coinbase Wallet, Exodus, and Tonkeeper. It also attempts to recover saved credentials from the phone’s keychain. If it finds a targeted wallet and the first exchanges with its server succeed, it attempts to upload wallet files, recovered keychain data, and photo thumbnails. Exposure of wallet files or credentials could put funds at risk.

It goes on to try to access messages, contacts, call history, voicemail, email, calendar entries, and cached location data. The payload can also contact its server for further instructions. 

The exploit chain was disclosed by Google back in March, with Apple issuing a patch later the same month. 

9to5Mac’s Take

The usual advice applies to protect yourself. Never visit links sent to you unless you trust the sender and are specifically expecting them. Always ensure that you install iOS updates as soon as they are available.

title: Apple’s Taptic Engine patent defeat sends litigation funder’s shares up 9%
snippet: Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Shares in litigation funder Burford Capital jumped more than 9% today as a result of Apple’s $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement. Here are the details.

Apple verdict lifts litigation funder valuation

Last Friday, a US jury ruled that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes on two patents held by California-based company Taction Technology.

Apple introduced the Taptic Engine in September 2014 with the first Apple Watch, and the technology has since expanded to other products, including the iPhone, where it provides haptic feedback for notifications, interactions, and other system events.

When Taction filed its patent infringement lawsuit in 2021, the company accused Apple of directly and indirectly infringing two of its patents through the Taptic Engine used in a range of iPhone and Apple Watch models.

Last Friday, following the verdict, Taction said the jury had “vindicated its patent rights,” while Apple said it strongly disagreed with the decision and would appeal.

Earlier today, as reported by The Financial Times, litigation funder Burford Capital disclosed that it has a financial entitlement in the case, and that it could be entitled to $1.4 billion if the $5.7 billion verdict is ultimately paid in full.

The disclosure sent Burford shares sharply higher in London, with the stock closing up 9.41% and giving the company a market capitalization of £659.9 million, or roughly $875 million.

Bloomberg Law notes that court records show that Taction received funding from Kenosha Investments LP and Gronostaj Investments LLC. The report also notes that Kenosha has been identified as an indirect subsidiary of Burford, which finances lawsuits in exchange for a share of any eventual recovery.

In a statement to investors on Monday, Burford said that if the $5.7 billion verdict were paid in full, its $1.4 billion entitlement would be split roughly equally between the company’s own balance sheet and its investment funds.

title: Motorola Signature 27 confirmed to support GrapheneOS
snippet: It’s confirmed: The mysterious Motorola phone getting support for the privacy-focused GrapheneOS will be the Motorola Signature 27 that was announced earlier this week. more…
fullText:
It’s confirmed: The mysterious Motorola phone getting support for the privacy-focused GrapheneOS will be the Motorola Signature 27 that was announced earlier this week.

GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused take on Android that’s grown popular in recent years, has so far only been available on Pixel devices. That’s for a number of reasons relating back to how Google handles the software and the security components in Pixel (and Tensor) hardware.

But, now, GrapheneOS is officially stepping beyond Pixel and into a device that will come pre-loaded with its version of Android. It was announced that this would be a Motorola device, but which device was left a mystery as all existing Motorola devices were not compatible with the platform.

Unsurprisingly, though, the first GrapheneOS device from Motorola will be the Motorola Signature 27. GrapheneOS confirmed the news on Twitter/X, though other details are still minimal. It’s apparently still planned that devices will be sold with GrapheneOS pre-installed. The Signature 27 was announced earlier this week and its use of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset is likely a major part of the reason it will be able to run GrapheneOS properly.

	

An exact release date for the Motorola Signature 27 has yet to be confirmed, and it’s unclear if GrapheneOS will be available right away either. It’s already known that future versions of Razr flip and Razr Fold will also support the privacy-focused OS.

fullText:

“Googlebook” is the name of Google’s new Android-based laptop platform, while “Google Books” is the company’s long-running index of books.

This is still happening as of today.

Searching for “Googlebook” doesn’t return the same error, but it’s a pretty funny result for Google’s own platform.

title: Final Cut Camera updated with support for iPhone 18 Pro features, more
snippet: Apple is rolling out a big update to Final Cut Camera today, the pro video app it first released for iPhone back in 2024. The update introduces a new design along with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple is rolling out a big update to Final Cut Camera today, the pro video app it first released for iPhone back in 2024. The update introduces a new design along with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro.

For those unfamiliar, Apple touts Final Cut Camera as a way to “record professional videos with full control of your footage and connect to Final Cut Pro for iPad to capture multiple angles at once with Live Multicam.” Apple announced the app in May 2024 and released it a month later.

Final Cut Camera version 2.4 is rolling out today with multiple key changes. First, it introduces a new, more customizable design with easier access to different settings.

The update also adds support for iPhone 18 Pro’s variable aperture, from f/1.48 to f/4, including shutter priority, aperture priority, and manual modes. It also supports Cinematic mode effects on iPhone 18 Pro, including video shot in ProRes and Apple Log.

With iPhone 18 Pro, users can take advantage of the new Fusion Main camera with variable aperture — the most advanced camera Apple has ever made — which brings aperture control to iPhone for the first time. Final Cut Camera allows creators to precisely dial in their aperture settings, or choose between shutter priority and aperture priority modes, to record stunning videos. The update also unlocks Cinematic mode effects for regular video, including footage captured in ProRes and Apple Log, allowing creators to adjust focus points and depth of field while editing in Final Cut Pro.

You can download Final Cut Camera on the App Store. The new update will start rolling out today. The app requires a subscription to Apple Creator Studio, which is $12.99 per month or $129 per year.

title: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra release over misbehavior & safety concerns
snippet: OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving. more…
fullText:
OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving.

The New York Times reports that OpenAI was planning to release GPT-6.1 Astra “in the coming days or weeks,” sometime in October, as its next major model release. GPT-6 Astra launched on September 3. GPT-6.1 Astra is said to have been “more capable” compared to GPT-6 in “completing challenging tasks from end-to-end without human assistance, as well as writing.”

The report cites an interview with Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, who confirmed that the model had regressed in two specific areas. Firstly, it “performed poorly on tests measuring alignment,” or how closely it sticks to the commands/prompts given by the human operator. Secondly, it showed “higher levels of deception,” not always telling the truth about the actions it did or did not take following a prompt. It was also added that GPT-6.1 Astra would push forward in a task beyond the current scope and without user permission, including interacting with external tools and/or services.

The new model would have been available in both ChatGPT and Codex.

	

OpenAI is due to have its annual developer conference, DevDay, tomorrow, where it’s very possible the company may have teased this new model update. Instead, the report explains, OpenAI will shift focus to “improving the safety of future models.”

This comes at a time when both OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slowdown in major AI development following recent breaches in GPT and Claude. Google’s Gemini also hacked into companies like those models, but stopped those actions faster than either of its rivals.

title: Google rolling out blood pressure & insulin resistance, more on Pixel Watch 3, 4, 5
snippet: As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics. more…
fullText:
As previewed during last month’s Pixel Watch 5 launch, Google is now starting to roll out blood pressure trends, insulin resistance trends, and sleep breathing quality metrics.

Health Guardian is Google’s overarching brand for the Pixel Watch’s suite of “proactive health and safety tools.” It includes Breathing Emergency Detection, which is available in Europe on the Pixel Watch 4 and 5.

The blood pressure trends feature works by passively measuring your pulse and motion patterns over the course of a month. It’s intended to let you detect “persistent higher cardiovascular trends early.” This works without a cuff or manual calibration, and was trained using billions of minutes of raw heart and movement data. You need “at least 5 consecutive days in a week” of data.

Insulin resistance trends analyze multi-week physiological data to track shifts in metabolic health without requiring a blood draw. Insulin resistance impacts how your body absorbs energy from food, with Google needing a minimum of 7 days of data in a month. The feature uses Google’s largest sensor foundational model. It was pre-trained using over 1 trillion minutes of data from 5 million opted-in users.

	
	

Both sets of trend insights will appear in the Google Health app on the first day of each month.

Meanwhile, sleep breathing quality metrics will track overnight breathing changes. In the morning, you’ll see how much time was spent optimally breathing, while a monthly report identifies longer-term patterns.

Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 users will be able to set up these three features in the Google Health app starting this week. Access is free on those three devices, with the first trend reports coming in early October.

If you’re a Google Health Premium subscriber, these three features are also coming to the Fitbit Air “later this year.”

title: Leak reveals new design details about Apple’s upcoming smart display
snippet: Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub. more…
fullText:
Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will have a 6-inch square display. The overall design is reminiscent of the iconic iMac G4, which featured a half-dome-shaped base with a metal arm holding up its display.

The device is said to be “about as thick as an iPhone” with quarter-inch, black bezels similar to older iPads. It has rounded corners with “no sharp edges,” Mark Gurman says.

Here are some more design details from the report:

It comes in Apple’s “standard gray aluminum finish” with a “rubberized bottom to help it stay on a table.”

It has a USB-C port for power and no built-in battery, so it must be connected to power at all times.

It sits on a “metal, round base with multiple rings of perforated speaker holes.”

The display connects to the base with a “polished metal arm.”

Users can tilt the display forward or backward.

There are no volume or power buttons.

There is a single front-facing FaceTime camera and no rear camera.

Bloomberg also says there’s a second version of the home hub that’s “designed to be mounted on a wall.” This version uses USB-C for power and has a “thin, square-shaped base beneath the display that houses the speakers and microphones.” The base reportedly “sits flat on the wall below the screen.”

You can read the full report at Bloomberg. What do you think of Apple’s home hub product? Are you planning to buy one (or multiple)? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Samsung’s Android 17 floodgates are open – updates rolling out for Galaxy S26, S25, more
snippet: The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone. more…
fullText:
The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone.

Samsung started testing its Android 17 update, otherwise known as One UI 9, back in May of this year. A delay behind the scenes left users waiting a bit longer, but it’s actually happening now.

That starts with Galaxy S26 devices, which are now widely receiving their Android 17 updates in regions all over the world. The update was already showing up for many in the US and South Korea, but it’s now appearing across Europe, India, and other regions as SammyGuru points out. Inbox by 9to5Google author Daniel Bader also notes that the roughly 4GB update landed on his Galaxy S26 Ultra in Canada earlier today. 

And the Galaxy S26 series is not alone.

	

SamMobile notes that stable updates are starting to appear for a host of other Galaxy devices, though right now in staggered releases and/or only for those who were previously enrolled in the beta program. Devices included in those early rollouts include Galaxy S25 series (including FE and Edge), Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy Z Fold 7, Galaxy Z Flip 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

Stay tuned as Samsung’s rollout expands – if history serves, we’ll be seeing a host of updates arriving in the coming days. Let us know in the comments if you see the update land on your device.

title: Google has fixed an issue that caused thousands of iPhone apps to crash overnight
snippet: An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied. more…
fullText:
An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied.

If you found apps on your iPhone or iPad were crashing last night, you’re not alone. Google confirmed last night that an issue with Analytics for Firebase was causing crashes when apps tried to launch. The issue was on Google’s end with an “incorrectly formatted payload” for the SDK.

You wouldn’t think of Google when a widespread crashing issue surfaces on iPhone, but Firebase is a valuable tool for developers on both Android and iOS, and is integrated into thousands of apps. The crashing issue was out of the developer’s hands and required a fix on Google’s end. The impact was huge, with some developers seeing tens of thousands of crashes – some far more – from their app’s users.

That fix has already been rolled out, Google confirmed.

	

Nick Cooke, a software engineer at Google, summarized a timeline of events:

Starting on Monday, 2026-09-28 at 17:41 US/PDT. Google Analytics for Firebase iOS+ experienced an issue causing crashes on launch due to an incorrectly formatted payload received by the SDK.

We fully rolled out a fix by Monday, 2026-09-28 at 19:52 US/PDT.

No SDK updates are required on your end to apply this fix.

Due to caching behavior, some app instances may still experience crashes for up to 4 hours after the rollout completed. These remaining cases should automatically resolve themselves by 2026-09-28 at 23:52 US/PDT.

At this point, crashing issues should be resolved. The patch for this problem was fully rolled out by around midnight Pacific Time last night; no app updates needed. Affected apps should be fully working again at this point.

9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

One of the many new features included in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature, which lets users get alerted when a website updates content they’re interested in. Here’s how to use it.

Safari can now notify you when webpages change

One of the most useful ways Apple has incorporated Apple Intelligence into macOS 27 Golden Gate is through Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature.

With it, users can ask Safari to monitor a webpage for specific changes and receive a notification when it detects an update.

When setting up a new custom notification, in addition to telling Safari what to look for, the user can also set a regular schedule ranging from hourly to monthly.

After the custom notification is set up, Safari will check the webpage according to the selected schedule and notify the user when it detects the requested change, such as a price drop, an item coming back in stock, changes to policies, registrations opening, or new information being added to the page.

Setting up Safari’s new “Notify Me” feature:

On Safari, go to the webpage you want to keep an eye on.

Click the Page menu button to the right of the Smart Search field.

Select “Notify Me” from the pop-up menu.

In the “What should Safari look for?” field, describe what you want. Apple Intelligence will then analyze the page’s contents to determine whether it can handle your request.

Optionally, you can set how often and when Safari should check for updates. Hourly and Daily let you choose a specific time, while Weekly and Monthly also let you choose specific days.

Click Done. Alternatively, Safari may show a Next button instead. In that case, macOS will ask for permission to send Safari notifications. You can also manage Safari notification permissions from Settings > Notifications > Safari.

Importantly, since the feature relies on Apple Intelligence, it may not be available in all languages or regions. To check the current availability status, follow this link.

title: tvOS 27 adds new reason to use profiles on your Apple TV 4K
snippet: Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles. more…
fullText:
Apple keeps improving its profiles feature on Apple TV 4K, and a change in tvOS 27 related to app access offers another reason to use profiles.

tvOS 27 lets you restrict users from launching specific apps

User profiles are a common feature of every major streaming service. They ensure viewers in a shared household can keep their viewing history and recommendations separate, among other benefits.

Apple has long had a profiles feature in tvOS, but it’s gotten a lot more useful in the past year thanks to several recent upgrades.

Now tvOS 27 has introduced another improvement. Per Apple’s official release notes:

Individual app controls in Settings let you block users from launching specific apps.

This change is clearly intended for parents. 

Profiles for children can already limit the types of content they’ll see in the Apple TV app. That’s a useful feature, but it won’t keep your child from opening a different app with no such restrictions.

	

Now though, parents can open Settings and block certain apps from being launched at all when a child’s profile is active.

It’s a good step toward making profiles as full-featured as they deserve to be, and aligns with Apple’s recent focus in iOS 27 on upgrading parental controls.

On the subject of profile improvements, iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 will bring Apple’s profile system to iPhone and iPad for the first time. You can read about that change here.

title: The ultra-pocketable ‘Picco’ e-reader from Boox is now up for pre-order, $99
snippet: The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order. more…
fullText:
The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order.

The Boox Picco has really only been teased here and there. We got a preview at IFA 2026, but we didn’t get to dive in as much as we wanted. The unit was still pre-production and in need of various refinements. Still, Boox has been in this game for a while, so we expect a good experience.

Today, Boox announced that Picco is now available for pre-order on its website. It starts at $99, but the website lists it at $109 for those purchasing from the US warehouse.

The Picco’s black-and-white display comes in at just 3.97 inches, and even still, it offers a front light for day and night reading sessions. It weighs just 58 grams, and even though Boox doesn’t list the device’s thickness in the press release, our own hands-on would tell us the tiny e-reader is plenty thin.

	

It will still add a little bulk to your phone if you choose to attach it with magnets. While it isn’t magnetic by itself, the Boox Picco comes with a case that makes it possible. It’s one of the most demanded features for the tiny e-readers that have already been released, because it adds a second screen without the doomscrolling and eye strain.

Another great detail to point out during the pre-order phase is that the Boox Picco doesn’t run Android, which we covered previously. This means access to third-party apps from the Google Play Store isn’t available. Still, a simple experience will allow users to transfer files with a companion app if you don’t want to use the SD card slot to manually move ePUB files.

Boox’s adorable little Picco is expected to ship out around October for those who pre-order.

title: Is That Early Holiday Deal or Fake Discount? Our Shopping Expert Chimes In
snippet: If you plan on shopping during early holiday sales, double-check prices before you buy.
fullText:
It’s hard to believe that the holidays are a couple of months away. 

Retailers, like Amazon and Walmart, are just a few of the stores with upcoming early holiday sales to discount popular gifts like tech, kitchen gadgets and toys. But oftentimes, you may wonder whether the sales are really worth it or if retailers are fooling you with fake discounts, inflated original prices and flashy sale badges to make you think you’re getting big savings. 

CNET’s latest holiday shopping survey found that US adults are already bracing themselves for frustrations just like that. In fact, 43% are frustrated by fake or misleading discounts, and 35% are worried about inflated baseline costs. So how do you spot a good deal from fake savings and discounts? Here’s how. 

			

More from CNET

Yes, early holiday sales are worth it

James Bricknell, CNET’s managing editor for deals, broke down how some retailers may try to show a deep discount that isn’t quite true — also known as inflating baseline or original prices. 

“Often, retailers will not inflate the price per se, but will inflate the recommended retail price to suggest the product sells for more than it does,” said Bricknell. “This makes the discount feel larger, when it may only be 5% or 10% off.” 

It’s one of the frustrations that over one-third (35%) of US adults expect when holiday shopping this year, according to CNET’s latest findings. Other shopping pains include deals selling out instantly (39%) and higher prices for outdated tech (33%). 

But that doesn’t mean you shouldn’t ignore holiday sales. It could be one way to save on a new device you’re considering, like a laptop or headphones — even if it’s not a deep discount. While some savings may be only 10 or 20%, they could still help shave off some of the cost and avoid paying full price. 

But with some retailers adjusting prices to falsify savings, how do you really know you’re getting a deal? 

How to spot a good deal during holiday sales 

Typically, early holiday sales yield savings on tech but you’ll need to create a plan and do some research before the sales start. 

Over the years, CNET has done the work to determine if sales are worth it and shared the best deals on popular tech items. We use several data sources to see when a product is truly on sale, compare the new price with a 90-day average, and share them during big sales, along with expert insight on some of the most popular gadgets to help you shop confidently.

You can take some of the same steps as our deals team by comparing prices across retailers to find the biggest savings.

“Don’t assume the first place you see has the best sale; shop around to make sure the sale price seems legit,” Bricknell said. 

If you’re worried about secretly higher prices, Bricknell recommends checking the brand’s official website for the base price. Once you find a good deal, use a price tracker like CamelCamelCamel or Keepa to see historical pricing and determine whether it’s worth buying now or waiting. 

Chrome’s Shopping Insights browser extension lets you bookmark a page and track a price. Google says that trackable products are saved to your Shopping list folder by default, too. And now Safari’s Notify Me tool is a built-in tool that can track webpage changes, including price drops. CNET also has a price comparison extension, though it’s probably faster to find what you want through our big roundups of deals during sales. 

Bricknell added that if a deal seems too good to be true, it probably is. “A deep discount of 50% or 75% on something that normally costs hundreds is something to be wary of.”

title: Amazon’s Carrie is a cyberbullying nightmare
snippet: Do we really need a new version of Carrie? That's the question that plagues any attempt to reimagine the classic horror tale. Stephen King's 1974 novel remains one of his most iconic, and the film version from Brian De Palma and Sissy Spacek two years later remains unsurpassed, despite a handful adaptations that followed in the ensuing decades. Any new iteration of the story bears the burden of proving why it needs to exist in the first place. Mike Flanagan's new Carrie series on Prime Video manages to do exactly that: It not only captures the terror and drama that has made the story so enduring, but updates it in a way that feels perfectly … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Do we really need a new version of Carrie? That’s the question that plagues any attempt to reimagine the classic horror tale. Stephen King’s 1974 novel remains one of his most iconic, and the film version from Brian De Palma and Sissy Spacek two years later remains unsurpassed, despite a handful adaptations that followed in the ensuing decades. Any new iteration of the story bears the burden of proving why it needs to exist in the first place. Mike Flanagan’s new Carrie series on Prime Video manages to do exactly that: It not only captures the terror and drama that has made the story so enduring, but updates it in a way that feels perfectly suited for 2026.

Carrie is also notable for coming from Flanagan, who has extensive experience both with King adaptations and limited horror series. He directed King-based films like The Shining sequel Doctor Sleep and The Life of Chuck, and became especially well known for putting out a string of shows on Netflix between 2018 and 2023, including the likes of The Haunting of Bly Manor and Midnight Mass. For years he helped Netflix own the month of October, so it was something of a coup when Amazon poached Flanagan with an exclusive TV deal in 2022. Carrie is the first project to come out of that partnership.

This version of Carietta White (Summer H. Howell), better known as Carrie, is a sheltered teenager who was largely isolated from the world until the death of her father. That event forced her and her mother Margaret (Samantha Sloyan) to reenter society for legal reasons, which for Carrie means attending high school for the first time. Despite a few changes here and there, Carrie tells the same basic story as its source material: A lonely young girl is met with the harsh realities of the world and is bullied to the point of awakening telekinetic powers that, ultimately, are unleashed with destructive force on a small town. The key beats remain in place, including Carrie’s most iconic scenes; Carrie is still pelted with tampons in a gym class shower when she gets her first period, and she’s still doused with pig’s blood at prom by a jealous bully.

But the Amazon show, by nature of being an eight-episode series, also expands on the story. And, much like Apple TV’s recent update of Cape Fear, some of the biggest changes are down to technology. When Carrie is embarrassed in gym class, the whole thing gets filmed, which then leads to the creation of an anonymous Instagram account — handle: “carriered” — that is used to bully her and, eventually, the whole school. Unsubstantiated rumors are given life by the account, including everything from teachers dating students to popular kids getting pregnant. What starts out as a bunch of mean-spirited memes turns into real-world consequences. Margaret, who in this iteration of the story is not only a religious zealot but also a conspiracy theorist, goes on to become a “parents’ rights activist,” fighting against the account with tactics that are eerily similar to those of right-wing influencers.

Flanagan is no stranger to using classic horror to explore modern issues. His final Netflix series, The Fall of the House of Usher, adapted various Edgar Allan Poe stories into a show that was ultimately about the opioid epidemic. Carrie’s modern twists feel much more natural, and smartly transform the story into one that explores just how nightmarish the high school experience has become with the advent of cyberbullying. It’s a kind of torment that follows you home, existing outside of the confines of a school, which in turn makes it that much more difficult for the school to police. Carrie is the perfect vehicle for this; she’s kind and unassuming and has little understanding of the outside world. Bullying is a confusing and terrifying experience for anyone, but its effects are heightened for an innocent kid like Carrie who simply doesn’t grasp why anyone would do this to her. She comes into the high school experience with hope and a little trepidation, and she leaves covered in blood as a town literally explodes around her.

Image: Amazon MGM Studios

The extra runtime in Carrie is also used to flesh out some of the characters outside of Carrie herself, most notably her mother and her main bully, Christine “Chris” Hargensen (Alison Thornton). Both have moments where they’re almost sympathetic. Margaret does want to help Carrie, she just goes about it in all of the worst possible ways, while Chris is portrayed as much more than just a rich kid lashing out. She’s dealing with an extremely troubled home life and doesn’t know how to handle it. She’s mean and cruel, but you also get the sense that she wants to change, even if she can’t seem to get over that hump. The show is helped by an excellent cast — which also includes school faculty played by Matthew Lillard, Amber Midthunder, and Rahul Kohli — that make these traditionally one-dimensional characters seem like real, believable people.

Almost all of the changes Carrie makes, which include some minor twists on the events of the story, are worthwhile. But there is one big exception. The show makes some heavy-handed gestures to the broader Stephen King universe of superpowered psychics — yes, at one point someone uses the word “shine” — which really starts to drag things down as it approaches its explosive finale. Not only does the addition feel unnecessary, and further complicates an already complex story, it also makes the grave error of taking away some of Carrie’s agency. I can’t say much more without delving into spoiler territory, but the change removes a lot of the punch from the finale.

Aside from that, Carrie manages to answer that difficult question about why it exists. It’s not only a largely great retelling of the classic story, but one that uses that familiar tale to dig deep into an important current topic. Its modern trappings aren’t superficial twists; they heighten what was already a dark and haunting tale. And they make this iteration as terrifying as any that came before it.

All episodes of Carrie will be streaming on Prime Video on October 7th.

title: Report: Apple working on new Vision Pro, with different form factors on the table
snippet: After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg. more…
fullText:
After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg.

Unlike the previous N100 project, it doesn’t seem the new project, N224, is necessarily targeted at being a lower cost offering. It could instead be a successor to the current M5-based Vision Pro model, though it might still come in at a lower price while offering the flagship experience.

This new version seems relatively early in the works, with Bloomberg reporting that it could arrive between late 2028 and early 2029. That said, it isn’t quite clear what exactly Apple will be going for. The company currently has four concepts in the works.

One of the concepts is similar to the recently unveiled Meta VR glasses, which offloads the compute and battery to an external puck. Given the fact that Vision Pro already has an external battery, offloading the compute doesn’t necessarily seem like a major hurdle, though you’d need better thermals and more efficient compute to pull that off.

On the other hand, some Apple executives reportedly don’t love the idea of an external puck, and “want the company to stick with something closer to an all-in-one design.”

Design wise, Apple might get a bit more experimental compared to the current Vision Pro, with the company supposedly considering other material choices. From the Power On newsletter:

One design in testing retains the basic egg-shaped form of the current Vision Pro, but Apple is actively exploring ways to reduce its weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials. The company has also continued to explore a standalone puck that combines the computing components and battery, similar to the approach used by Meta’s recent VR Glasses.

Wrap up

Time will tell what Apple will actually end up delivering. title: Apple hit with $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement
snippet: Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions. Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents. more…
fullText:
Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions.

Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents.

As reported by CNBC, the lawsuit centered around two patents:

U.S. Patent No. 10,659,885

U.S. Patent No. 10,820,117

Both patents are focused on a “vibration module for applying vibrational tractions to a wearer’s skin.” Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes upon its patents, saying that Apple was “capitalizing on Taction’s innovation and success.”

Apple’s Taptic Engine first debuted as part of the Apple Watch in 2014 and came to the iPhone 6s and iPhone 6s Plus the following year, replacing the older vibration motor.

In a statement, an Apple spokesperson said:

“While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today’s verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts.

Apple’s Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology, which Taction’s own testing of Apple’s products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction’s technology, and we will appeal.”

Taction Technology is a California-based company that describes itself as being “obsessed by sound.” The company says that its “Transporter Technology powers the game-changing Corsair HS60 Haptic headphones, and will soon be powering other premium headphones from major manufacturers.”

In a statement to CNBC, Taction’s lead counsel said:

“We’re happy the jury found for Taction and vindicated its patent rights. Taction waited five and a half years for this case to get to trial, so it was a long time coming.”

You can read the original complaint for patent infringement filed by Taction here and Friday’s jury ruling here.

title: DoorDash’s drone strategy started on the ground
snippet: DoorDash unveiled the six-propeller aircraft that will be used in its new drone delivery business at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event.
fullText:
When DoorDash set out to build a drone delivery business, it started with the tricky logistics that happen on the ground before it looked up.

The autonomous drone came last, according to the company, which unveiled its new six-propeller aircraft at its annual Dash Forward 2026 event on Wednesday. 

Before DoorDash worked on the aircraft, the company focused on ground infrastructure, including loading systems, how food would be handed off from a restaurant’s kitchen, and packaging.

DoorDash Labs, the R&D team that built its autonomous sidewalk delivery bot Dot, created the drone delivery service now called DoorDash Air. The same team also developed the underlying software, called the Autonomous Delivery Platform (ADP), to handle the coordination challenges in deliveries handled by humans, sidewalk delivery bots, and now drones.

The ADP software uses smart routing, incorporating factors like weather, flight range, and ground traffic to narrow down which orders actually make sense to send by air.

Image Credits:DoorDash

The company’s systems-first strategy for its DoorDash Air business aligns with its strengths. DoorDash isn’t a hardware company, but it is sitting on 13 years of user data from the merchant and customer sides of the business. (DoorDash has previously disclosed that more than 500,000 restaurants are on its delivery marketplace.)

The company says it sized the whole DoorDash Air system around its historical order data, including how much orders weigh and how far they typically travel. 

“We didn’t start with a drone and ask what would fit,” Harrison Shih, who heads up DoorDash Air, said in a statement. “We started with what people order and how local businesses actually operate, then built the entire system from there.”

DoorDash announced plans in July to launch the drone delivery business after receiving a Part 135 air carrier certification from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration. The certification allows the company to legally operate a commercial drone delivery service in the United States.

The drone, which has six slow-spinning propellers mounted at the ends of its arms, is equipped with a winch to pick up, carry, and drop off packages. 

DoorDash said it plans to kick off early pilot deliveries in Northern California with partners including Chipotle, Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, and Momo N Curry.

title: Microsoft quietly ending ‘Copilot+ PC’ branding for Windows laptops
snippet: After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops. more…
fullText:
After a couple of years of relentlessly pushing it, Microsoft is seemingly ending its Copilot+ PC branding for Windows laptops.

Windows Central spoke with executives from Microsoft and Qualcomm about the lack of Copilot+ PC branding on the latest Surface machines. While it’s not been said explicitly, Surface CVP Brett Ostrum all-but-confirmed the end of that branding by saying:

…these are not called Copilot+ PCs. They do meet all the requirements of our previous bar for what Copilot+ devices are. We still lean into the narrative around AI on the edge and being able to have a hybrid solution out there.

	

Copilot+ PC branding was generally used to identify a laptop that met certain hardware requirements around AI features, particularly the NPU, which virtually every mid-high-end laptop already supports. Windows Central further points out that Nvidia’s RTX Spark push has been absent of any mention of Copilot+ PC branding.

Microsoft started using this branding back in 2024, but when the flagship feature of the Copilot+ PC, Recall, was met with backlash, the branding became little more than a hardware checkbox that consumers didn’t fully understand. 

	

The only big question left – does this mean the Copilot Key is going away?

title: What even is a ‘microdrama’?
snippet: On Monday, Variety reported that RoseBerry Media is recutting episodes of the Australian soap opera Neighbours "into microdramas." These clips will be available on Epis, a short-form vertical video streaming platform. Though Neighbours ran for 41 seasons from 1985 to 2025, at launch, RoseBerry is only recutting two storylines from the late aughts focused on a character played by the now-internationally famous Margot Robbie. In a statement about the project, RoseBerry cofounder / CEO Guy Hameiri described Neighbours as "an iconic piece of television history" that's well suited to be adapted for vertical viewing with the company's proprietar … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
On Monday, Variety reported that RoseBerry Media is recutting episodes of the Australian soap opera Neighbours “into microdramas.” These clips will be available on Epis, a short-form vertical video streaming platform. Though Neighbours ran for 41 seasons from 1985 to 2025, at launch, RoseBerry is only recutting two storylines from the late aughts focused on a character played by the now-internationally famous Margot Robbie.

In a statement about the project, RoseBerry cofounder / CEO Guy Hameiri described Neighbours as “an iconic piece of television history” that’s well suited to be adapted for vertical viewing with the company’s proprietary, AI-powered production workflow. Hameiri also said that he believes the project will demonstrate how “premium vertical television will become a significant new entertainment category” — one that can help introduce new audiences to a classic series.

Variety’s framing of RoseBerry’s new vertical cut of Neighbours as a kind of microdrama is curious. Microdramas are short-form vertical videos often featuring characters who get caught up in convoluted romance plots, which makes them somewhat similar to Neighbours in terms of their shared subject matter. But unlike network television shows with sizable budgets, microdramas are produced on the cheap and crafted specifically to be consumed on mobile. And when you factor in how microdramas tend to adhere to a narrative formula that opens with intrigue and closes on melodramatic cliffhangers, it’s easy to see the format as a storytelling genre unto itself.

Over the past year, entertainment trades’ reporting has made it seem like Hollywood is ready to go all in on microdramas, and that these kinds of projects could help the industry bring much-needed production work back to Los Angeles. It’s unclear whether Variety’s phrasing is reflective of the industry’s definition of microdramas changing, or if studios are just trying to use buzzwords to drum up hype. But if microdramas really are going to be a key part of Hollywood’s future, we should probably all have a general understanding of what they actually are.

Both the amount of money that went into Neighbours and the quality of the cast’s acting make it a very different kind of entertainment compared to the microdramas that have become hits for companies like ReelShort and DramaBox. What RoseBerry is doing with Neighbours is much more akin to what Tattle TV did with Alfred Hitchcock’s silent film The Lodger: A Story of the London Fog earlier this year, and what startup Snips is doing with series like Big Brother and MasterChef. While there might be an audience for these things, it feels somewhat disingenuous to lump them in with the campy, bite-sized series like Forbidden Fling With My Bestie’s Dad that defined and popularized microdramas as a format in the West.

Microdramas originated in China, where they first began gaining traction around 2018 on platforms like Douyin and Kuaishou (both TikTok analogs). Kuaishou’s Unexpectedness — a satirical comedy about a man struggling to achieve his goals — was one of the first Chinese microseries to make a splash, and as the social video platforms embraced e-commerce, brands began to see microdramas as a viable way to market their products to viewers. As the audiences for microdramas grew, more Chinese film / TV production studios began producing microdramas, and by 2021, revenue from short-form video was projected to hit $500 million. That figure was expected to hit $7 billion by 2024 and $16.2 billion by 2030.

Though microdramas in all languages tend to be seen as lower-quality entertainment, their core appeal is fairly easy to grasp. The series lean heavily into well-established narrative tropes, and their stories are usually designed to leave viewers guessing about what kind of outlandish twists they’re about to see next. Microdramas’ verticality and the way they’re served up in short minuteslong segments makes them the sort of content that’s meant to be consumed through a phone screen. Microdramas’ relatively small production budgets also positioned them to become a viable way for up-and-coming actors and filmmakers to book consistent work. But in recent months, that promise has been waylaid by the spread of generative artificial intelligence.

In China especially, gen AI has had a devastating impact on the microdrama economy for human actors. Ninety-five percent of the Chinese microdramas produced in the first three months of this year were created with AI, which has led to fewer jobs and lower pay. A similar story is now playing out in Hollywood, where actors have reported being pressured by studios to sign over the rights to their digital likenesses. Though the details are somewhat different, presenting repurposed films and TV series as “microdramas” poses a similar threat to the people working in the business because of the way it cuts them out of opportunities like RoseBerry’s partnership with Epis. It’s also unclear how and whether this new vertical presentation of Neighbours might result in royalty payments to the show’s original cast and crew.

Streamers and studios’ interest in vertical content of all kinds has been driven by a desire to recapture some of the attention lost to rival platforms like TikTok and YouTube where microdramas have been able to thrive. For the most part, studios have been leading with repurposed, verticalized clips of preexisting content, which are presented in scrollable feeds that are meant to give you a preview of things that can be watched horizontally. These feeds’ content might be useful for discovery, but very much like microserialized (read: chopped-up) films and TV shows, they aren’t exactly a new entertainment format that seems worth making much noise about.

Traditional microdramas haven’t even really had a chance to live up to all the industry hype, but it feels like companies are already rushing to redefine the format as anything that happens to be short, dramatic, and vertically oriented. Platforms might be more interested in turning old shows and films into clip content because it’s less expensive than producing and building an audience for a wholly original microdrama. That doesn’t lend credence to the idea that this format can actually “save” Hollywood, though — if anything, it makes the industry seem like it’s trying to cannibalize itself.

title: AirPods Pro 3 vs AirPods 5: Three reasons to go Pro
snippet: Apple debuted the all-new AirPods 5 this month, and they bring ANC to lower prices than ever before. If you’re shopping for AirPods, however, there are still several reasons you might want to opt for the more expensive AirPods Pro 3. fullText:
Apple debuted the all-new AirPods 5 this month, and they bring ANC to lower prices than ever before. If you’re shopping for AirPods, however, there are still several reasons you might want to opt for the more expensive AirPods Pro 3.

Buy AirPods Pro $234 (Reg. $249)

Buy AirPods 5 $129

Buy AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case $149

Different design

AirPods are one of Apple’s most personal products. The fit can vary dramatically between different people depending on the size of their ears. AirPods 5 offer an open-ear design, so they rest on the inside of your ear. AirPods Pro, meanwhile, offer a more traditional in-ear design with ear tips.

Personally, I find AirPods Pro to be more comfortable than AirPods 5. They’re also more secure for me, so I’m less worried they’ll fall out of my ears.

Heart rate monitoring

One of the key differentiators between AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods 5 is that AirPods Pro 3 offer built-in heart rate monitoring capabilities. During a workout, AirPods Pro can measure your heart rate to provide additional fitness metrics.

If you wear an Apple Watch, AirPods Pro 3 work along with your Apple Watch to ensure you get the most accurate data possible. Apple’s algorithms monitor the data from AirPods Pro and Apple Watch, and factor in the type of workout you’re doing, to use the most consistent data possible. For example, if you’re lifting weights and the Apple Watch ends up at an awkward angle on your wrist, AirPods Pro 3 will step in to provide more accurate data.

Furthermore, in iOS 27, Apple brought GymKit to the iPhone, so you can use iPhone and AirPods to get an Apple Watch-style experience … but without wearing a watch. Learn more about this change in Zac’s full coverage.

Hearing Aid

AirPods Pro 3 offer a range of hearing health features that aren’t available on AirPods 5. This includes:

Hearing Test

Hearing Aid

Hearing Protection

With the Hearing Test feature, you can take a 5-minute test to identify if you have hearing loss. Apple’s Hearing Aid feature, meanwhile, is a clinical-grade hearing aid that uses the results of your test to craft a sound profile for your needs. Finally, Hearing Protection, can help prevent exposure to loud environmental noise.

Wrap up

There are other reasons to choose AirPods Pro over AirPods 5, including longer battery life, even better ANC, and a more capable charging case. The difference in ANC, in particular, is notable: Apple says AirPods Pro 3 offer 3x more Active Noise Cancellation than AirPods 5.

snippet: Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series. more…
fullText:
Following Direct My Call and Hold for Me, Google is introducing “Call for Me” on the Pixel 11 series.

	

Reminiscent of Google Duplex, this Gemini Intelligence feature is officially an “early experiment” to let Google handle “routine phone calls” to book appointments, place items on hold, and reschedule reservations. Examples include 

reserve patio seating at a restaurant

check if a hardware store has a specific part in stock

move your haircut appointment to next Thursday

Google says it will “respect the time of the neighborhood shops and front-desk staff answering the phone,” and that “calls made by Gemini on behalf of the user represent real customers conducting real transactions.”

Asking AI to speak on your behalf is a big step that requires genuine trust. That’s why we built this experience around user control.

Your Pixel 11 will “call on your behalf using the Gemini app.” Users see a live transcript and can take over at any point.  Gemini will “introduce itself” and “handle the conversation with the person on the other end.” As part of this, it can wait on hold and navigate any automated phone menus.

	

Google is “starting small to get the experience right.” As of today, an early preview is rolling out to Gemini subscribers using the enrolled in the Phone by Google beta on the Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and 11 Pro Fold in the US. More details are available here.

title: Google brings back Android Dev Summit with Android 18 ‘powerful new graphics features’ tease
snippet: The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18. more…
fullText:
The Android Dev Summit is returning in 2026 after Google’s last focused developer conference in 2022. Additionally, the agenda comes with a mention of Android 18.

The last Android Dev Summit was in 2022. The developer-focused event is now back with two days of programming at Google’s headquarters in Mountain View, as well as a satellite “Extended” event in London.

There will be a “keynote with Android leadership on the latest features and updates.” There are four conference tracks: AI experiences, Android XR, Apps foundation, and Tools and performance. 

Meanwhile, we get our first mention of Android 18, including how there will be “powerful new graphics features.”

	

“Elevate your apps with the latest graphics features in Jetpack Compose and Android 18” is a particularly interesting session:

Ready to take your Android UI from “it works” to “it’s a work of art”? 

	

Join us for a tour of the latest graphics capabilities in Jetpack Compose. We’ll show you how to build new visual effects, from delightful mesh gradients to progressive blurs, and using the powerful new graphics features in Android 18. We will also show you how to improve the performance of your graphics features, without sacrificing battery life or frame rates.

It will be interesting to see if Android 18 is announced at or just before the conference. Android no longer has developer previews in light of the Canary channel. But for reference, Android 16 testing began in November. Any sort of Android 18 preview in October would be very early.

Android XR and AI are big focuses, with notable sessions about how to:

Connect your apps to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system: “Explore how to connect your applications seamlessly to Gemini, Search and the Android intelligence system.”

Integrate your app with the Android intelligence system: “Android is evolving into an intelligence system where agents like Gemini orchestrate tasks across apps… We’ll also explore proactive experiences using the Android Context Engine.”

Building audio-first experiences for intelligent eyewear with Gemini Nano 4

The Android Dev Summit takes place on October 28-29.

title: Anker’s 25W MagSafe 3-in-1 packs active cooling in a travel-sized design [Hands-on]
snippet: If you’re rocking an iPhone 16 or newer, you might be interested in a Qi2.2 charger to take full advantage of the 25W MagSafe charging speeds that your phone can support. Anker’s new 25W Prime MagSafe 3-in-1 is one of many great options, and it comes in an excellent portable design. more…
fullText:
If you’re rocking an iPhone 16 or newer, you might be interested in a Qi2.2 charger to take full advantage of the 25W MagSafe charging speeds that your phone can support. Anker’s new 25W Prime MagSafe 3-in-1 is one of many great options, and it comes in an excellent portable design.

Impressions

The big trend of the latter half of 2025 was bringing 25W Qi2.2 to every single wireless charging accessory possible, and that’s continued through 2026. Anker is kicking things off with a new portable MagSafe 3-in-1 that packs 25W Qi2.2 support into a very portable design.

With 25W of wireless charging, active cooling is practically a necessity. Nearly every 25W charger on the market integrates it, and the new Anker foldable 3-in-1 is no exception.

In the box, you get a 45W charge brick and USB-C cable – providing ample power to charge your iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch all at once. With this stand, you can charge an iPhone 18 Pro to 50% in just 27 minutes.

Remember MagSafe Duo? If you were someone who really enjoyed that product before Apple killed it off, you’ll likely enjoy this one. It has extremely similar portability characteristics, but comes with two key benefits: it can serve as a stand, and it can charge three devices at once instead of two.

One neat (though totally unnecessary) feature on this charger is that the Apple Watch charger is spring-loaded. It does fold inwards while you have the charger compacted, but when you’re ready to unfold everything, you just need to press downward on it and it springs outward. I thought that was pretty neat, and helps justify the premium price tag that this product demands.

Wrap up

All in all, if you want a nice MagSafe 3-in-1 charger that can easily work for travel, this new Anker offering is a great choice. Since it includes active cooling, it actually charges your iPhone rather quickly without any of the overheating or other negative side affects that wireless charging can sometimes have.

Anker’s new 3-in-1 MagSafe is available on Amazon with Prime delivery for just $99 currently, in both colors: black and white.

title: M6 Mac release schedule: Here’s when to expect new Macs
snippet: Apple next-generation M6 chip arrived last week in the new Mac mini. But several more products will get M6 upgrades soon. Here’s the rumored release schedule for M6 Macs—plus the M6 iPad Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple next-generation M6 chip arrived last week in the new Mac mini. But several more products will get M6 upgrades soon. Here’s the rumored release schedule for M6 Macs—plus the M6 iPad Pro.

This fall: M6 MacBook Pro, M6 iMac

This fall, likely in October or early November, Apple is rumored to launch two new M6 Macs:

MacBook Pro

iMac

The MacBook Pro will be only the 14-inch base model. Per Mark Gurman, Apple is skipping Pro and Max versions of the M6 chip. As a result, only the entry MacBook Pro will get M6 while the next Pro-level chips coming will be M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple’s new iMac isn’t expected to change much beyond the M6 chip. The only other rumored upgrade is a fresh slate of colors. But the jump from M4 to M6 should make the new model a worthy update nonetheless.

Notably absent from this list is the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra. It’s expected to launch soon too, but will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead of the M6.

Early 2027: M6 MacBook Air, M6 iPad Pro

After this fall, the next products rumored to get M6 upgrades are:

MacBook Air

iPad Pro

A new M6 MacBook Air is expected to launch in early 2027. Anytime in the February-April window is possible, but based on Apple’s history, March is a safe bet.

Other than a chip upgrade, there are minimal rumors about the new MacBook Air. It should retain the same design as the M5 model. And reporting dates an OLED upgrade as coming no sooner than 2028, so the display will likely be unchanged too.

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it got the M5 chip. Rumors point to a spring 2027 update coming, meaning the product will follow its typical 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond getting the M6 chip, Apple’s new iPad Pro is expected to add a vapor chamber for cooling. That should boost sustained performance in the ultra-thin device.

One potential M6 benefit for both the MacBook Air and iPad Pro is that it could boost battery life. Apple says the M6’s 2-nanometer process brings “a major leap in performance and power efficiency.”

snippet: Deadline reports that Apple TV recently recorded its biggest week ever for viewership, fueled by its 29 Emmy wins and recent releases such as Ted Lasso and Mayday. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Deadline reports that Apple TV recently recorded its biggest week ever for viewership, fueled by its 29 Emmy wins and recent releases such as Ted Lasso and Mayday. Here are the details.

Apple TV sees record viewership following the Emmys

A few weeks ago, Apple TV broke its own record with a total of 29 Emmy wins, 14 of which went to surprise hit Widow’s Bay.

Around the same time, Apple TV subscribers also got the return of Slow Horses, alongside recent releases including the Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh-led Mayday and the much-anticipated fourth season of Ted Lasso.

According to Deadline, this perfect storm helped Apple TV record its “highest weekly viewership ever for the week of Sept. 14, rising by +67% year-over-year.”

From Deadline:

Released straight-to-streaming on Sept. 4, Mayday has become Apple TV’s biggest film debut on the platform to date over its first 18 days, the company said. In the U.S., Mayday opened at No. 1 in Luminate’s Sept. 4-10 weekly rankings with 8.7M views. It remained strong in Week 2, placing at No.2.

The site also notes that, according to Apple TV, Widow’s Bay saw a whopping 280% week-over-week increase in viewership during the week after the Emmys, where it took home 14 awards, including Outstanding Comedy Series.

Apple TV noted that the increase was particularly notable in “the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Brazil, Mexico, Germany, India, Poland, and Spain,” says Deadline.

The company added that Pluribus saw a similar effect following its six Emmy wins, including Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for Rhea Seehorn. The series “experienced a 200% surge in viewership week-over-week following the ceremony,” according to Apple.

Finally, Deadline notes that while the Emmys and recent premieres certainly helped drive the gains, Apple’s recent iCloud+ expansion may also have played a role.

Earlier this month, Apple began including Apple TV with iCloud+ at no extra charge in more than 100 countries, a rollout that also brought the streaming service to 59 new markets for the first time, expanding its total reach to 170 countries.

To read Deadline’s full report, which also includes data from Nielsen and Luminate, follow this link.

fullText:
This week saw the debut of Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon chips and, with it, the usual onslaught of Tensor hate around Google’s Pixel phones. Personally, I don’t care about those, but new launches around Qualcomm’s event have shown off a lot of other specs I’d much rather see Pixel adopt.

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every Sunday along with ‘Inbox’ on Tuesday and Thursday. You can find past issues here.

Google’s Tensor chip in Pixel phones has been a hot-button issue for enthusiasts for the entire time Google has been working on the project. And, I get it. Tensor is objectively not as powerful as a flagship Snapdragon or MediaTek chip and, with Pixel phones getting more and more expensive, that’s hard to accept. Google has solved many of the biggest deficiencies, leading to fairly wide acceptance from the “average Joe” customer base that Google is aiming for in the first place, but every year the same conversation comes back up with a new Snapdragon chip – “I wish that was in my Pixel.”

Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 family – I’m choosing to not put “Extreme” into that word salad here – looks incredible, and MediaTek’s new Dimensity 9600 Pro is also going to be solid. It’s totally okay to be annoyed that Pixels don’t get the same raw horsepower.

	

But, for me at least, it’s everything else that I wish Google would get a bit more on board with.

This week’s new chip launches also saw the announcement of new phones using those chips and, man, it’s wild how much faster these other brands are progressing compared to market staples like Pixel and Galaxy. The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Oppo Find X10 look insane. 

Xiaomi 18 Pro series goes official with ‘privacy screen,’ 8,500 mAh battery, and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6

Oppo Find X10 series goes official with triple 200MP cameras, 8,000 mAh battery

8,000+ mAh batteries, a plethora of 200MP cameras, that’s the sort of stuff I wish I was getting on my Pixel. Forget horsepower, give me battery life and camera sensors that look good even before the power of computational photography steps in. The Oppo Find X9 Ultra was a big wake-up for me in that regard, as it was the first phone in quite a while that made me want to ditch the Pixel from my phone lineup (and I’m sure our Inbox author Daniel Bader is greatly enjoying it after prying it from my “Techtember”-ed fingers).

Google, if you’re listening, the rest of the Android world is frankly killing it on the hardware front right now. The software is still so-so in my book, but the practical wins that come from these all-out builds are too great to ignore. So, Pixel 12 maybe? Thanks.

This Week’s Top Stories

Googlebook is here – what do you think?

Following a tease earlier this year, Google took the wraps off of its Android-based Googlebook platform. Five laptops, deep smartphone integration, and prices starting at $899. I’m personally skeptical, but I’m very curious to hear what you think about the new initiative.

Next year’s Android chips are here

As mentioned earlier, Qualcomm and MediaTek both made big announcements this year, those being their respective new chipsets for Android flagships. Qualcomm has a pair of Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chips, one more powerful than the other, while MediaTek has a Dimensity 9600 Pro alongside a variant designed for the “flagship killer” segment. title: Gemini fully replaces Google Assistant on Android
snippet: At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out. more…
fullText:
At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out.

Google has been moving Assistant users to Gemini over the past few weeks. This deprecation was originally set for 2025 and later extended to 2026. In early August, Google announced the final timeline.

From various user reports today, this migration appears to be fully underway. Google Assistant is gone on all devices/accounts we checked in the US and Europe.

	

Notably, the Gemini app has removed the “Switch to Google Assistant” setting. This shortcut no longer appears at the bottom of the account menu with Google app 17.60 stable and 17.62 beta.

	

As such, you can no longer “use or switch back to Google Assistant on your phone, tablet, or paired devices.” The latter grouping includes Wear OS, headphones, and Android Auto.

There are no changes to Assistant just yet on “Google Nest and Google Home smart speakers, displays, or other Google Assistant-enabled speakers and displays.”

Gemini is now the “voice assistant experience on Android” when you long-press the power button or swipe from the corners.

title: Apple and Amazon face renewed UK antitrust lawsuit
snippet: A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A UK tribunal has allowed part of a renewed antitrust lawsuit against Apple and Amazon to move forward, over allegations that the companies restricted competition for Apple and Beats products sold on Amazon. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Back in 2023, Apple and Amazon were hit with a proposed UK class action over a 2018 agreement that allegedly restricted which third-party sellers could offer Apple and Beats products through Amazon’s marketplace, reducing competition and, as a result, driving up prices for consumers.

It is worth noting that the UK was not the only market where the agreement drew scrutiny. Apple and Amazon have faced antitrust investigations and legal challenges over similar reseller restrictions in countries including Italy, Spain, Germany, and the United States.

In the British lawsuit, a class representative led by consumer law academic Christine Riefa accused the companies of reducing competition and driving up prices for consumers buying Apple and Beats products in the UK.

Last year, however, Britain’s Competition Appeal Tribunal refused to certify the case, citing concerns about how the lawsuit was being financed and about Riefa’s ability to independently protect the interests of the class.

The court took particular issue with the fact that, under the funding agreement, Asertis (which was financing the litigation in exchange for a success fee) could potentially have been paid out of any damages award before consumers received anything. The tribunal said the arrangement could even have resulted in the class receiving no damages at all.

From the decision:

“Our overall impression was that Prof Riefa was extremely reliant on her legal

advisers. We were not convinced that she had properly understood the

arrangements into which the PCR had entered on behalf of the Proposed Class

Members, and we were concerned about her ability to protect the interests of

the class robustly and independently.”

And

“Our key concern in this case is that Prof Riefa has not demonstrated sufficient

independence or robustness so as to act fairly and adequately in the interests of

the class.”

In its conclusion, the tribunal said a class representative cannot be “merely a figurehead” for proceedings being conducted by their lawyers, and that they should “act as the independent advocate for the class.”

The claim was later refiled by a new proposed class representative, Justin Le Patourel, which brings us to today.

UK tribunal allows part of lawsuit to proceed

As reported by Reuters, Britain’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today allowed part of the refiled lawsuit to proceed, while narrowing the case to claims involving Apple products purchased through Amazon’s marketplace.

From Reuters:

The tribunal allowed claims ​relating to Apple products bought through Amazon’s marketplace to proceed, but rejected ⁠one covering those bought directly from Apple and other retailers.

And

Judge Kelyn Bacon said claims relating to Amazon marketplace purchases were “plausible, credible ‌and ⁠grounded in the facts”, but rejected wider claims relating to other retailers because they rested on a “complex and speculative theory of harm”.

Reuters says the portion of the lawsuit now allowed to proceed could be worth between £289 million and £306 million, including interest.

Commenting on the decision, Apple told Reuters that its agreement with Amazon was intended to curb the sale of counterfeit products, and maintained that it “strongly” disagrees with the lawsuit.

Amazon, in turn, said it is confident the remaining claim will prove to be “without merit” as the legal process moves forward.

Finally, Reuters says a spokesperson for Le Patourel “welcomed the ruling, but said it was disappointing ​that parts ⁠of the claim were not certified.”

title: Bose launched wired, yes, wired, earbuds with ANC for $99
snippet: The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device. more…
fullText:
The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device.

Bose wants to get back to basics, it seems – it just launched a new pair of wired earbuds with ANC, citing a rise in wired listening popularity. The earbuds connect to any USB-C device, using an internal, proprietary DSP to ensure they work in just about any USB-C port. With any source input, the earbuds output a fixed 24bit signal.

Bose is well-known for its Quiet Comfort lineup in recent years, but it didn’t start there. Still, the company can be considered one of the main players responsible for quality ANC in wireless headphones. After all, the QC35’s became the go-to travel option for some time.

This release, however, has literal strings attached. It needs USB-C to operate, not a 3.5mm output as most wired enthusiasts prefer at a minimum. That means you wouldn’t be able to use your own DAC/amp setup.

	

Even still, Bose’s Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds will be a good option for those who need ANC without the battery anxiety. Bose says the earbuds have two microphones on each bud to power active noise cancellation. Quiet Mode blocks most noise out, and Aware Mode acts as a transparency setting. ANC can also be disabled.

The new wired Bose earbuds are available to pre-order starting today for $99 in Black and White Smoke. Bose says the buds will begin shipping on October 15 for those who order from the official website and Best Buy.

title: Google confirms Photos bug that prevents editing and deleting, fix coming ‘ASAP’
snippet: Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way. more…
fullText:
Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way.

Various user reports on Reddit last week confirmed that a recent glitch has been preventing users from interacting with images after they’ve been edited. That includes sharing, adding to galleries, deleting, and re-editing photos, all from changes as simple as cropping an image. Luckily, Google confirmed in a statement with Android Authority — which reported on the app issues late last week — that a fix is being worked on, with the team working to roll it out “ASAP.”

The Google Photos team is working on rolling out a fix ASAP! […] For now, users can try these 2 workarounds: 1) Tap “Save as copy” when saving new edits, and 2) Visit photos.google.com to delete or share already-edited photos.

Until these changes are live, the company recommends either saving your image as a copy when creating new edits (to prevent locking up the original, sole copy of an image) or accessing the web version of Photos to share or delete as needed.

While I can’t say I’ve seen this bug on my own Pixel 11 Pro XL, it does appear that most of the affected users — or at least those reporting the issue online — are sporting the last few generations of Google’s Tensor-powered devices. If you’ve found yourself in that group, keep an eye on the Play Store for an update coming soon.
