title: MacBook Pro redesign is coming, with three features we’ve waited years for
snippet: Apple has a big MacBook Pro redesign in the works (possibly called MacBook Ultra) that’s expected to launch in October. Here are three rumored new features that we’ve waited a long time for. more…
fullText:
Apple has a big MacBook Pro redesign in the works (possibly called MacBook Ultra) that’s expected to launch in October. Here are three rumored new features that we’ve waited a long time for.

#1: OLED display

It’s hard to overstate the value of display technology for a product that many users spend all day looking at. Yet for years, the Mac has lagged behind Apple’s other products in offering the most cutting-edge display tech.

OLED has been a mainstay on iPhone for years, and iPad Pro introduced a tandem OLED in 2024 that many Mac users pined for. Now with the new MacBook Pro, OLED is finally coming to Mac.

The redesigned MacBook Pro with OLED is expected to offer truer blacks, improved contrast, and likely help out with battery life too. Here’s hoping it’s able to match the impressive tandem OLED the iPad offers.

#2: Touchscreen

Apple has long argued that the Mac doesn’t need a touchscreen, despite competing products nearly all offering touch. But rumors indicate we’re finally getting the first Mac with touch support.

The new MacBook Pro will have a touchscreen, and macOS 27 is already packed with hints that such a feature is coming. We’re expecting further software optimizations to make touch feel like a natural experience on the Mac.

Despite touch being available, macOS will remain tailored primarily for trackpad and keyboard input. Touch will be a secondary tool on the Mac, not replacing traditional input methods but rather supplementing them for users who have grown accustomed to touchscreens on iPhones, iPads, and PCs.

#3: No more notch

When Apple last redesigned the MacBook Pro in 2021, it introduced a notch design that first came to iPhone. The notch then spread to the MacBook Air too, making it a fixture of modern Mac design.

	

But the new MacBook Pro will reportedly drop the notch in favor of a hole-punch camera cutout that likely resembles what we’ve seen on iPhone Duo.

The Dynamic Island will be brought over to macOS too, making the camera cutout integrate seamlessly on the Mac like it does on iPhone. As someone who finds the notch more of an eyesore on the Mac than I ever did on iPhone, I’m excited to see the notch disappear soon.

title: Google combines Material 3 Expressive & Liquid Glass on the iPhone [Gallery]
snippet: With Liquid Glass now a year old, Google apps on iOS are beginning to incorporate the translucent material alongside its Material 3 Expressive design language. more…
fullText:
With Liquid Glass now a year old, Google apps on iOS are beginning to incorporate the translucent material alongside its Material 3 Expressive design language.

Previously, the Google Photos floating bottom bar on iOS had a solid background, just like the Android version. As of version 7.94, it’s now made of Liquid Glass.

The screenshots on the left show the “Default” translucency level, while the “More clear” option is on the right and lets you see more of the image behind it. With the dark theme, you see how the default blue accent color tints the current tab indicator.

Google has also updated buttons in the top bar with Liquid Glass.

	

The traditional bottom bar in Google Health has also been updated with Liquid Glass. You can see what’s under the navigation element, while the “Ask Coach” FAB (floating action button) gets a frosted treatment.

The company is still in the process of phasing out the previous Google Material Theme design language on iOS with Material 3. Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Keep have been stragglers, while Tasks was updated fairly recently.

More broadly, Google has shown no interest in adding Dynamic Color to its iOS apps. It could add a manual system that lets users choose an accent color across all Google apps. That said, without system access to the wallpaper, it’s a bit pointless, with Dynamic Color always more of a system-level Android feature.

title: The new Kindle ditches the raised bezel in a push toward a smaller, lighter e-reader
snippet: The new Kindle lineup features its lightest and thinnest designs yet, with a sleek, front-flush display that eliminates bezels for good.
fullText:
Amazon is giving the Kindle its most significant physical redesign in years, introducing a refreshed lineup of e-readers built around a deceptively simple idea: getting rid of the raised bezel.

The redesigned Kindle unveiled Thursday replaces the traditional raised bezel surrounding the display with a flush-front design, creating a cleaner, more seamless look. But bezels also give readers a place to rest their fingers without accidentally touching the screen and triggering a page turn or another touchscreen command. Amazon says it has designed around that problem.

At a press briefing, Kevin Keith, Amazon’s vice president of devices, said the company is using “Cap” (capacitive) touch technology and haptics to create what he describes as a “dead zone.” As a reader grips the Kindle, the device detects where a finger is resting and adjusts the touch-sensitive area accordingly.

“When you’re gripping the Kindle, wherever you put your thumb, it will self-detect a dead zone in the Cap touch. It will just readjust, and it’ll know that the finger is there,” Keith said.

Image Credits:Amazon

Alongside the bezel-free redesign, the standard six-inch Kindle is now 6.8 millimeters thick and weighs 140 grams, making it both thinner and lighter than its predecessor. Amazon is positioning it as the most pocket-friendly Kindle in the lineup.

Amazon said the new display is also 30% faster at page turns than the previous generation. The lineup also introduces new colors, including Ube, Alpine Sky, Seaglass Green, Graphite, and Fig.

The new Kindle starts at $149.99 and is available in Ube and Graphite. For the first time, Amazon is also offering an aluminum-backed version, with 32GB of storage and color options, including Alpine Sky and Seaglass Green.

Image Credits:TechCrunch

The redesign extends to the Kindle Paperwhite, which is also thinner and lighter than the previous generation.

Amazon describes the Paperwhite as having the largest display in the Kindle lineup, along with the highest contrast ratio. The company says the combination is designed to deliver “deep blacks and crisp text, and images that pop off the screen, whether you’re reading in bright sunlight or under the covers at night.”

The standard Paperwhite comes with 16GB of storage and costs $199.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition costs $249.99 and is available in Graphite and Seaglass Green.

The Kindle Colorsoft, which Amazon introduced in 2024 as its first Kindle with a color display, also adopts the thinner, lighter, flush-front design used across the refreshed lineup. The standard Colorsoft has 16GB of storage and starts at $289.99 in Graphite. A 32GB Signature Edition is available in Graphite and Fig for $319.99.

Image Credits:Amazon

The new Kindle and its aluminum version are available starting today in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Brazil, the U.K., Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Sweden, Poland, Japan, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, and Australia.

The new Kindle Paperwhite and Kindle Colorsoft are available for preorder across the same regions.

Amazon is also continuing to offer its Kids lineup. The Kids Kindle is currently available for purchase, whereas the Kids Kindle Colorsoft is available for preorder in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., Germany, and Japan.

title: Gears of War: E-Day is a great game launching at a terrible time
snippet: There are few blockbuster games that are as confident as Gears of War: E-Day. A prequel to one of Xbox's most transformative titles, E-Day knows exactly what it wants to be: a brutal, tense, and self-aware action game, one that is stronger because it doesn't deviate from that premise. Twenty years since the original Gears of War, there's still nothing like its particular brand of up-close cover shooter gameplay, and E-Day shows that it still hits hard two decades later. As Xbox moves into a messy new era focused on its biggest franchises, E-Day could be an early glimpse at the future of the platform. But it's also launching during one of the … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
There are few blockbuster games that are as confident as Gears of War: E-Day. A prequel to one of Xbox’s most transformative titles, E-Day knows exactly what it wants to be: a brutal, tense, and self-aware action game, one that is stronger because it doesn’t deviate from that premise. Twenty years since the original Gears of War, there’s still nothing like its particular brand of up-close cover shooter gameplay, and E-Day shows that it still hits hard two decades later. As Xbox moves into a messy new era focused on its biggest franchises, E-Day could be an early glimpse at the future of the platform. But it’s also launching during one of the most tumultuous periods in Xbox history.

Set 14 years before the original Gears, E-Day tells the story of a pivotal point in the franchise’s sci-fi lore: “emergence day,” the moment when a collective known as the Locust Horde revealed itself with a surprise attack designed to wipe out the entire human race. You play as a slightly younger, but still gruff and experienced, soldier named Marcus Fenix as he and his squad attempt to fight back against the subterranean extraterrestrials. Marcus is part of an elite group known as “gears,” which are basically really buff guys and gals that wear massive armor and are thrown into action when things get really bad.

Things don’t get much worse than the events of E-Day. The human planet Sera is absolutely annihilated by the horde, which launches attacks from holes in the ground and has carved out a labyrinth of underground tunnels that allow them to strike anywhere. Marcus and his squad are thrown into the fray, tasked with doing everything they can to fight back and help where they’re able. Missions have you attacking enemy strongholds, escorting important supply caravans, and searching for survivors amid the rubble. Over the course of the game you see the planet turn from a retrofuturistic paradise to the ruins of a lost civilization.

E-Day is reminiscent of a James Cameron film: Absolutely every element is in service to creating a thrilling sci-fi spectacle. It’s as close to a playable Aliens as you’re bound to find. The cover shooter action remains visceral; everything has a weight to it, from Marcus’ slow movements to the chunky feel of reloading a shotgun. E-Day nails the sense of being pinned down in the middle of a war, surrounded on all sides, being terrified you’ll run out of bullets before the enemy does. There’s an unparalleled sense of tension.

E-Day does an excellent job of mixing things up so that you aren’t spending the whole game hiding behind chunks of concrete or burned-out husks of cars. There are huge set-pieces where the world crumbles around you as gigantic creatures lay waste to the city, and eerily quiet moments where you wander through a dark tunnel or foggy cemetery, unsure of what terrors await. E-Day has some side missions, but its world is largely linear, pushing you through one sequence after another with pacing that never really lets up. It’s all rendered with a lavish attention to detail on everything from the way blood splatters on the camera after a particularly gruesome kill to the outline of a leather wallet in the back pocket of Marcus’ jeans as he’s forced into combat in civilian clothes.

This conceit also means that, much like Avatar and its sequels, E-Day’s story is to the point and straightforward. Cutscenes give you just enough detail to care about the characters when dramatic things happen, but don’t get in the way of the action. No, the series hasn’t reached the emotion promised by the memorable “Mad World” commercial, but it doesn’t need to. In fact, much of the writing feels intentionally stupid, driving home that this is, at its very core, a dumb action game. The amount of ridiculous one-liners in the game approaches an art form, with pivotal moments punctuated by lines like “A giant floating ballsack with glowing eyes is trying to kill us!” or “Hold on to your dicks!” The true spiritual energy of E-Day can be found in its barks, those lines tossed out by Marcus and his comrades as they mow down bad guys. Here are a few examples:

“Too ugly to live.”

“Where are you going? I thought you wanted some of this.”

“Rest in pieces.”

“It ain’t your day, asshole.”

“Looks dead to me.”

“Lights out, fuckface.”

“How do you like that, you stupid-ass spider bitch?”

Image: Xbox Game Studios

That’s just a sampling. There’s a strangely joyous nature to the dialogue. The game is violent, the story is dire, but you’re still meant to enjoy the action of firing big guns and using a chainsaw to cut monsters in half. It feels good to play, and the campaign puts you through a range of emotions — at points it even approaches horror, with pitch-black tunnels teeming with bloodthirsty creatures — while never letting go of its action core. E-Day is a 2006 version of Gears rendered with the technology of 2026, which I mean as a total compliment: It’s a pure action game that isn’t saddled by modern trends.

It is also launching at an especially challenging time. Xbox is in the midst of “reset,” in which new CEO Asha Sharma is gutting the division, slashing around 3,200 jobs, and dramatically shaping how its current studios operate, with the ultimate — and perhaps unattainable — goal of focusing entirely on Xbox’s biggest franchises to reach a billion players. In a certain light, E-Day is indicative of this new approach, even if it predates Sharma’s time in charge. After launching tentpole franchises like Forza and Halo on the PlayStation 5, E-Day appears to represent a shift back to Xbox console exclusives. In essence, it’s a big, boisterous return for an iconic series, one that you can only play on Microsoft platforms. If you wanted an idea of what the future of Xbox could look like, E-Day offers an enticing vision.

I’m not entirely confident that the future will play out like that. Xbox’s strategic plans shift constantly, and E-Day developer The Coalition was hit with at least one layoff before launch, and staff fear more are coming. Xbox’s new leadership says that it wants to “focus on higher priority projects,” which on the surface sounds a lot like a bold, confident return for Gears of War. That’s exactly what you get with E-Day, but it might not be enough for whatever comes next for Xbox.

Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6th on the PC and Xbox.

title: iOS 27 makes a great change to Apple Pay on iPhone
snippet: Apple has redesigned the Apple Pay checkout flow in iOS 27 for apps and websites. The changes make it easier to switch between different payment cards and see key details about the order you’re placing. more…
fullText:
Apple has redesigned the Apple Pay checkout flow in iOS 27 for apps and websites. The changes make it easier to switch between different payment cards and see key details about the order you’re placing.

In iOS 27, you can now swipe between payment cards right on the main Apple Pay interface. You can also tap a card to view a grid-style interface that shows all your available Apple Pay cards in one place.

Apple explains:

Apple Pay is introducing an updated design for users when they check out on the web and in apps. The design allows them to seamlessly swipe to switch cards, conveniently surfacing important information about their eligible cards in Apple Wallet — including rewards, balances, debit account balance, pay later options, and more — so they can make more informed payment decisions.

Merchants and developers have control over what appears on the Apple Pay payment sheet, depending on the exact information they need to complete your order.

The iOS 26 version of the Apple Pay checkout flow has been criticized for being unintuitive. For instance, people often tapped the wrong thing when trying to switch between payment cards. The instinct is to tap the card itself, but in iOS 26, that would take you to the address-editing interface. You’d have to tap a separate button at the bottom to actually switch to a different card. iOS 27 streamlines all of this and makes it a lot clearer.

title: ‘Carrie’ Review: Mike Flanagan’s Remake Is a Timely (and Terrifying) High School Tragedy
snippet: Prime Video’s Carrie is a poignant, emotional retelling of Stephen King’s classic horror story.
fullText:
There’s a new Carrie in town. The upcoming horror series from Executive Producer Mike Flanagan (creator and director of Netflix’s The Haunting of Hill House) aims to introduce the tragedy of young Carrie White to a new audience while offering die-hard fans a new perspective. All eight episodes land on Wednesday on Prime Video, and I’m sure the heated fan discussions will follow.

It’s been 50 years since Brian De Palma’s movie adaptation of Stephen King‘s debut novel hit theaters. Carrie follows the story of a misunderstood girl with psychic abilities who is bullied at school and abused at home until things come to a bloody and fiery end. The film made Sissy Spacek a star, turned King’s book into a bestseller and set the stage for him to become the prolific, iconic genre writer we know today.

Read more: Prime Video: The 31 Absolute Best Shows to Watch

			

More from CNET

This isn’t the first reincarnation of the Carry White story. There was a sequel, two movie remakes and even a stage musical all inspired by her story. Now, it’s Flanagan’s turn to tell the tale, and the result is a layered, in-depth study of how grief and trauma can shape and destroy a strong mother-daughter bond.

Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan as Carrie and Margaret White in Prime Video’s Carrie.Liane Hentscher/Prime Video

Further, it’s an exploration of how a broken education system and unchecked abuse, through social media of all things, can lead to the unraveling of an awkward girl who just wants to exist in a world that shuns her at every turn.

The first big departure for the show from the movie is its narrative structure. De Palma’s movie runs 98 minutes; Flanagan’s series is roughly three times longer, which gives the story a chance to breathe and allows him to expand on the overall world it takes place in.

As I mentioned above, school plays a huge part in the series. We get insight into the lives of the faculty, their struggles in teaching the students, while also balancing their own demons. And since it is modern-day, there’s an assortment of added details like social media bullying and interference from strong-willed parents.

I regularly imagine what my own high school experience would’ve been like if everyone had a smartphone in their pocket, ready at a moment’s notice to record someone being bullied and share it online. That’s a big component here, and, without spoiling much, it is an instigator, sparking the fire in Carrie that inevitably leads to the bloody climax at prom. However, there are also tributaries that extend from this social media abuse that impact the high school and the community at large.

High school showers are the worst.Prime Video

If you’re at all familiar with Flanagan’s work, you’ll know he is attracted to emotionally deep stories. His version of Carrie spends a lot of time establishing the relationship between Carrie and her mother, Margaret White, who, in the original movie and book, is presented as an evil religious zealot. Piper Laurie’s performance as Carrie’s mom is iconic, unhinged and downright terrifying.

Instead of going in that direction, here, this iteration of Carrie builds a complicated, loving relationship between mother and daughter. The introduction of school and the outside world leads to a breakdown of that bond, as Carrie begins to discover and eventually lean into her power.

Summer H. Howell’s performance as Carrie is utterly heartbreaking. Her ability to wear her emotions on her sleeve and cycle between childlike innocence and unbridled rage is the necessary energy that steers the series where it needs to go. She’s simply transcendent in the role. 

When did Margaret White become the voice of reason anyway?

Samantha Sloyan’s take on Margaret White is an absolute surprise, though. I knew going into this that she’d deliver a memorable performance, considering the work she did as devout zealot Bev Keane in Flanagan’s Netflix series, Midnight Mass. She brings a similar energy to the role of Margaret, but instead of dialing up the god-fearing madness, this version of the character is delightfully nuanced.

I found myself relating to her and even rooting for her, which wasn’t something I had on my bingo card going into this.

As for Carrie’s peers, the ensemble cast delivers. Sierra Agudong’s Sue Snell offers a conflicted voice of reason amid the unfolding madness. Alison Thornton’s exploration of Chris Hargensen is filled with sadness and an unfettered thirst for power, as her semblance of normalcy crumbles.

Just two high school girls hanging out, not doing anything troubling at all.Robert Falconer/Prime Video

Young female relationships populate the series, which has led to concerns I’ve read online that this will once again be a Carrie told through a male’s eyes. Yes, Flanagan’s name is on the project and, yes, King is the one who penned the original tale, but a lot has changed since the De Palma movie first premiered. 

His film still holds a place in cinema, but all you need to do is revisit the famed locker room scene in which Carrie gets her first period, and you’ll see a lot of nudity, which is troubling, considering the fact that these women (actresses all of legal age) were still portraying underage high school girls.

Aside from Flanagan contributing as a writer and director on the series, Prime Video’s Carrie features an array of female writers (Elizabeth Padden, Justina Ireland, Dani Parker, Alexandra Magistso and Rebecca Leigh Klingel) and directors (Kate Siegel, Axelle Carolyn, Kyra Sedgwick and Hiromi Kamata), which gives the story a new perspective. 

Finally, the tragedy of Carrie White is told through a necessary female gaze, and, in the process, the conflicts that arise resonate on a deeper, more authentic level.

By the time we get to the prom, the storm of blood, fire and death hits in a much different, impactful way.

Carrie is technically a horror series, but there’s a lack of gore and violence featured throughout most of the series. That may sound like a flaw, but it’s a detail that only adds to the emotional experience. Take away the supernatural aspect of the story, and you’d be left with a poignant coming-of-age tragedy that ticks all the binge-worthy boxes of a streaming series worthy of your time. But this is a Mike Flanagan joint, so what else are you expecting?

title: This is my top feature request for the upcoming A20 Pro iPad mini
snippet: For the past year, we’ve been looking forward to a new iPad mini refresh, and it’s sounding like its just around the corner. A new leak last week from Aaron Perris unveiled that the product should feature an A20 Pro chip and thinner bezels, and we already know it’ll feature OLED and a water resistant design. fullText:
For the past year, we’ve been looking forward to a new iPad mini refresh, and it’s sounding like its just around the corner. A new leak last week from Aaron Perris unveiled that the product should feature an A20 Pro chip and thinner bezels, and we already know it’ll feature OLED and a water resistant design.

While those upgrades are excellent, I have one major thing I want from the next iPad mini, and it has to do with software.

After seeing the iPhone Duo, I’m amazed at how well Apple mastered the multitasking on the device. Multitasking on iPad has always felt like a mess to me, and iPhone Duo just feels elegant.

On such a small screen, having proper windowing on the iPad mini never felt appropriate. Users likely aren’t overlapping many windows on iPad mini. That’s why I want Apple to steal one nifty feature from the iPhone Duo: split screen with picture in picture.

	

I mean really, this is such an excellent experience. Currently, there’s no way on iPad mini to make a picture in picture window take up the entire width of the device in portrait, and even if there were, you’d either have to have it block some of your app, or manually align the sizing using windowing.

Bringing video and app split view to the iPad mini‘s display seems like a no brainer to me, especially given the fact that the iPhone Duo and iPad mini share similar aspect ratios. At least personally, I’d use an iPad mini in portrait a lot more if this feature existed.

snippet: Amazon continues its move away from Android on Fire TV, with its latest Fire TV Stick 4K moving over to Vega OS, though with upgrades including support for using your TV’s USB port for power and a massively improved remote. more…
fullText:
Amazon continues its move away from Android on Fire TV, with its latest Fire TV Stick 4K moving over to Vega OS, though with upgrades including support for using your TV’s USB port for power and a massively improved remote.

Available starting today, the new Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K costs $59.99 – $29.99 as a part of Prime Day deals next week. The new streamer, Amazon touts, is around 20-40% faster in most tasks compared to other 4K streaming devices and TVs while also being smaller than prior generations.

One welcome upgrade here is that you can power the new Fire TV Stick 4K using your TV’s USB port, making it a whole lot easier to power the streamer.

Amazon is also debuting a new remote here which has an asymmetric design that’s flat on top and rounded at the bottom. It has a metal home button for easy recognition, a customizable Star button, and IR controls for your other TV hardware such as a soundbar. Amazon is also launching a standalone version of this remote for other Fire TV devices.

	

The big change compared to the last generation, though, is that the latest Fire TV Stick 4K ditches Android in favor of Vega OS. Amazon’s new platform is indeed faster and continues to add more apps in time – Amazon says over 2,000 apps have been added this year – but it also loses support for sideloading, a popular option among many Fire TV users.

As mentioned, the new Fire TV Stick costs $59.99 and is available for purchase starting today in the US.

title: Google aware of Android Auto bug that blocks calls if your foldable phone is closed
snippet: An Android Auto bug is reportedly blocking outgoing calls from closed foldable phones, like the Motorola Razr. Both Google and Motorola are aware of the issue, which might mean a fix for those affected soon. more…
fullText:
An Android Auto bug is reportedly blocking outgoing calls from closed foldable phones, like the Motorola Razr. Both Google and Motorola are aware of the issue, which might mean a fix for those affected soon.

There is no shortage of form factors in the bucket of Android foldable devices. The most iconic might be the Razr from Motorola, if only for the nostalgia associated with it. Just like the original Razr flip phone in the mid-2000s, and every other foldable, the outer display has at least some use cases. Making or taking calls is a big one.

According to a couple of reports on Motorola and Google forums, the Motorola Razr can’t actually make calls while the phone is closed and connected to Android Auto because of a strange bug (via Android Authority). If an outgoing call is attempted, Android Auto throws an error that suggests opening the phone. When open, outgoing calls go through without issue.

Obviously, that negates the benefit of having a foldable device. And storing your foldable phone somewhere in your car while the internal display is exposed might be neglect, at least, in line with Samsung and Motorola’s suggested care.

	

The bug reports only mention calling from a Motorola Razr connected to Android Auto, ranging from the Razr Ultra 2025 and Razr Ultra 2026.

According to those users, there is a fix. The good news – reverting back to Google Assistant from Gemini solves the problem. The bad news – Google Assistant was just fully removed from Android as a whole on September 28.

Both Google and Motorola are aware of the Android Auto bug. Motorola’s thread lists a response from the company less than two weeks ago. It’s possible the bug is still affecting users, and with Gemini taking over for Google Assistant, the issue might only spread to more users and devices until a fix is widely rolled out.

Are you able to make Android Auto calls while your foldable phone is closed? Or is it working now?

fullText:

The Last First: Winter K2

When: October 2

What: Movie

Genre: Documentary

In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that unpacks the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, mountaineers John Snorri Sigurjónsson, an Icelander, and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. title: Apple Notes keeps getting better, here’s what’s new in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 adds new features for CarPlay, the Messages app, and a lot more, including a handful of Apple Notes upgrades. Here’s what’s new for Apple Notes in iOS 27. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 adds new features for CarPlay, the Messages app, and a lot more, including a handful of Apple Notes upgrades. Here’s what’s new for Apple Notes in iOS 27. 

Divider line added for organizing your notes

Joining the many different formatting tools already available in Apple Notes, iOS 27 lets you add divider lines to your notes.

It’s pretty simple. Just tap where you want the line to go, open the edit menu, and choose the new ‘Insert Divider Line’ option.

Divider lines are a great new way to organize content in a note, and a welcome addition to the Notes toolset.

Section links

Section links are now supported in iOS 27’s Notes app, letting you build a table of contents or other structure to navigate longer notes with ease.

To create a section link, select text inside your and open the edit menu. From there, hit ‘Add Link’ to see a new option: Link to Section.

This opens a menu where you’ll find all of the headings and subheadings currently found in your note. You can tap to select one, which will create a direct link to that section embedded in your text.

Create and add to notes with Siri AI

The single Notes upgrade I’m most excited about in iOS 27 involves Siri.

Apple’s new Siri AI lets you quickly, seamlessly add information to a new note or existing note in Apple Notes.

You can do this, for example, with any answer Siri provides in the new Siri app. Or you can do what I did (seen above) where I asked Siri to take a poorly formatted list and reformat it, then add it to a new note.

This works for existing notes too, just tell Siri which note you want to add to. Siri has offered some limited Notes capabilities in the past, but the new integration is a big upgrade.

Copy and paste Markdown

Last year in iOS 26, Apple Notes gained support for importing and exporting Markdown.

If you’re unfamiliar with Markdown, it’s a text formatting syntax created by John Gruber. With Markdown, you can write in plain text using special syntax for headings, links, lists, bold and italics formatting, and more. It’s a popular tool for writers who publish content online.

With iOS 27, Apple Notes is getting even more Markdown-friendly.

Now when you paste Markdown-formatted text into a note, it’s automatically converted into rich text. There are zero extra steps required. And if you want to copy text from your note as Markdown, there’s a new Copy as Markdown option you’ll find in the edit menu.

Image Playground upgrades

iOS 27 brings big upgrades to the Image Playground app and its underlying AI models. And since Image Playground is a key built-in feature of the Notes app, Notes users benefit too.

Per Apple’s press release:

Image Playground offers new powerful ways for users to bring their imagination to life. They can create high-quality images in virtually any style, now including photorealistic, thanks to a new generative model that runs on Private Cloud Compute. This is a major transformation for image generation across platforms. And generated images will automatically include a hidden SynthID watermark to identify them as AI-generated.

Apple Notes in iOS 27: wrap-up

Notes also features a variety of smaller UI refinements in iOS 27, including:

Newly refreshed app icon

Liquid Glass updates for buttons, menus, and more

Shared folder at top of folders list adds new icon

Individual shared folders and notes have updated icons too

title: The iPhone 18 Pro: The best and final iteration of the current form factor?
snippet: There’s a running joke that Apple always breathlessly announces that each year’s iPhone Pro is “the best iPhone we’ve ever made,” as if that were in some way surprising. But I do think that there’s some poignancy to the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumors about next year’s model are true, this could be the final iteration of the form factor that began with the iPhone X back in 2017. Specifically, we’re expecting next year to see the next big step toward that “single slab of glass” vision which will end the era of evolutionary change we’ve seen over the last decade … more…
fullText:
There’s a running joke that Apple always breathlessly announces that each year’s iPhone Pro is “the best iPhone we’ve ever made,” as if that were in some way surprising. But I do think that there’s some poignancy to the iPhone 18 Pro, because if the rumors about next year’s model are true, this could be the final iteration of the form factor that began with the iPhone X back in 2017.

Specifically, we’re expecting next year to see the next big step toward that “single slab of glass” vision which will end the era of evolutionary change we’ve seen over the last decade …

The evolution of the iPhone Pro models

If you were to line up every model from the iPhone 12 Pro to the iPhone 16 Pro, I think many people would struggle to tell the difference visually bar the switch from notch to Dynamic Island in 2022. The iPhone 17 Pro is still only an exception due to the extended camera island and Cosmic Orange option.

Of course, each model had new features, but I think even here it’s fair to say that unless a specific one has particular relevance to you personally, you really need to jump at least two or three generations before an upgrade amounts to a significantly better experience.

This in no way a criticism of Apple. The reality is that premium smartphones are a mature technology, at least in the conventional form-factor. We don’t see massive differences between successive generations because there’s only so much that can be done to improve them on an annual basis.

Apple is now experimenting with different form factors, starting with the iPhone Air and now, of course, the iPhone Duo – and we’re expecting another major design leap next year, in the form of a 20th anniversary model.

How exactly Apple will position next year’s design remains somewhat unclear. It was initially suggested that it would be a standalone model, distinct from the iPhone 19 Pro, while other reports suggest that it will be next year’s Pro model. There’s also the question of whether Apple will use sequential numbering or skip a number to mark the occasion, so it might instead be called the iPhone 20 Pro.

Personally, I do suspect that it will be the new iPhone Pro design, whether Apple calls it the 19 or 20. If this is correct, then the iPhone 18 Pro will be the final iteration of the form factor we’ve had for half a dozen years. 

I’m jumping two generations from the iPhone 16 Pro, so I’m going to separately list the new-to-me features introduced by each year’s models. I’m skipping improvements I see as trivial or completely irrelevant to my use, like 7-core GPU over 6-core and GenLock.

iPhone 17 Pro features carried forward

Center Stage front camera, for photos and video calls

Ultra-stabilised video

Dual capture

Telephoto lens up from 5x to 8x 

Telephoto sensor up from 12 MP to 48 MP

ProRes RAW video

Better battery life

Faster charging

New to iPhone 18 Pro

Wider maximum aperture on the main camera lens

Variable aperture main camera lens

Pro camera controls (aperture, shutter speed, white balance, histogram)

Photographic Styles v3

Smart focus tracking

Cinematic mode effects from standard video

Tap to zoom and rotate on the front camera

Smaller Dynamic Island, enabling three live activities

(Even) better battery life

(Even) faster charging

My personal … focus

Personally, there are five features I will be focusing on in my early usage.

Variable-aperture lens

While the headline feature is that variable aperture lens, I’ve said before that we probably shouldn’t expect too much from it. The maximum aperture is only marginally wider on such a small sensor, so I’m not expecting to see much difference in terms of shallow depth of field.

However, the maximum aperture does let in a little more light, amounting to around two-thirds of a stop. How much difference that will make remains to be seen, but it should translate to shorter Night Mode exposures. Since this is a feature I use a lot, often handheld, then I am looking forward to trying this.

Pro camera controls

The ability to control shutter speed will definitely have its uses for things like panning shots. And it will certainly be useful to be able to take full control of white balance. I’m also expecting the histogram to be useful when manually setting the exposure.

Photographic Styles v3

I’m generally not a filters kind of guy when it comes to either taking photos or editing them on the iPhone, preferring to do any editing using conventional adjustments afterwards. For that reason, I rarely used the existing Photographic Styles feature and don’t expect to make much use of the latest iteration either. But I must say I am intrigued by the film setting, so I’ll certainly be experimenting with this.

Smart focus tracking

One of the biggest weaknesses with autofocus when it comes to video occurs when the subject briefly passes behind something else and the camera can switch focus to the obstruction. Smart Focus Tracking claims to solve this problem, so I will certainly be putting this to the test.

Cinematic Mode effects from standard video

	

It’s less than a couple of months since I said that Apple appeared to have forgotten about Cinematic video mode. I said that was a great pity because, if Cinematic Mode video worked well, it would be an absolute game-changer for the practicality of the iPhone as a camera for more serious video work. So far, it has been frustratingly close but no cigar.

However, it appears I was wrong: one of the new iPhone 18 features is that the cinematic video effects can be applied to videos shot in standard mode.

It’s certainly very handy that we no longer need to decide in advance whether or not to use the mode, but what most interests me is that Apple is again paying attention to the feature. This suggests that it is indeed being shown some love, and we therefore can expect it to continue to improve in much the way Portrait mode did for still photos. I’m very much looking forward to testing this.

These, then, are the features I think could potentially make the most difference to me. How about you? If you’ve upgraded to the iPhone 18 Pro, what features drove your decision? Please share in the comments.

title: Ionna Charging Network Doubled to Over 180 Sites in 2026. Its CEO Tells Us What’s Next
snippet: The fast charging network founded by eight automakers is now said to be the largest 400 kW fast charging network in the US.
fullText:
Ionna — one of the newest EV fast-charging networks in the US — has had a heck of a growth spurt during its first year of operation. This week, it announced that it now has more than 180 live sites nationwide, more than doubling its footprint since the start of 2026. According to the company’s reckoning, that makes Ionna “the largest 400-kilowatt fast charging network in the US,” a very specific claim worth examining. 

I spoke with Ionna CEO Seth Cutler about the network’s rapid expansion, the new features rolling out and what Ionna is doing to make DC fast charging even more affordable for EV drivers.

Ionna was founded in July 2023 as a joint venture among seven major automakers: BMW, General Motors, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis. Later, in July 2024, Toyota joined the venture as an investor, bringing the total to eight companies on the board. The fledgling network opened its first “Rechargery” — the brand’s name for its brightly colored, retro-styled fast charging stations — in Apex, North Carolina, in December 2024. 

Less than two years later, Ionna’s network now includes more than 180 stations with over 1,500 charging ports across 30 states.

		

			

Largest 400 kW network*

From that first station in Apex, every Ionna Rechargery site has featured plugs for both the Combined Charging System and the North American Charging Standard, reducing the need to fiddle with adapters. The Rechargeries are also noteworthy for their standardization of high-powered 400-kW charging stalls. That’s faster than the average EV on sale in the US can accept, so drivers are less likely to find their charging sessions throttled when plugging in.

“We’ve built out a network for the future at 400 kilowatts,” Cutler told me during a video call. “New vehicles are coming with much higher native charging speeds — the BMW iX3 is a good example, as well as some Lexus and Toyota products coming to market soon. This network is built for them. Right now, we’re the largest 400 kW network and expect to continue to be for some time.”

That “largest 400 kW network” boast is an interesting one. Ionna is far from the largest DC fast charging network in the US. Tesla’s Supercharger network has had a 12-year head start and comprises over 3,000 locations — about half of all DC fast-charging ports in the country — across all 50 states. Second and third places go to EVgo and Electrify America, with about 1,200 and 1,000 sites, respectively.

However, those networks typically top out at around 325-350 kW, with some older stalls as low as 50-150 kW. That’s good enough for most of today’s EVs, but Ionna’s higher-powered bet may matter more down the road. Plus, it’s a very specific “largest” trophy for the brand to claim.

No app, no problem

During my recent EV road trip, I decided to stop by one of Ionna’s new Rechargeries in Sacramento, California. Before setting out, I tried to grab the requisite app and set up my account — as you would with every other EV charging network — and was amused to find that Ionna doesn’t have a proprietary app. There’s a web portal where you can search for stations, but the entire payment process takes place at the plug. Cutler says this decision was all about removing friction.

“When we first started the company, we asked, ‘What’s the first thing you need?’ and everyone put their hands up and said, ‘We need a charging app,’” Cutler recalled. “The problem we had was quantifying the why. Why do you need an app? What we’ve found is that the No. 1 reason people ask about an app is to know where our chargers are, but no one’s asking for an app because they want to pay better or pay more easily. We really want to remove friction, not add friction to the ecosystem.”

Ionna stations support both NACS (pictured) and CCS charging standards at up to 400 kW.Ionna

Instead, Ionna chose to work on integrating with 19 partner platforms, including recently announced collaborations with Presto, ChargeHub and EV Connect. For payments, the network focused on Plug & Charge support and Tap to Pay. Plug & Charge is a payment tech that lets drivers start charging and automatically pay simply by plugging their car into a compatible station. Ionna announced that it’s enabling compatibility with Volvo Cars, with Toyota and Lexus to follow in October. That will bring the total to nine automakers that can Plug & Charge, including Rivian, which is not on the Ionna board.

The new Driver Dashboard

Drivers also have the option to simply tap a credit card at the stall. (As a reviewer who is often charging fleet vehicles, this is my preferred method, and the Rechargeries I’ve visited are about as close to a gas station payment experience as I’ve had with an EV.) 

Cutler told me that most drivers who use Ionna stations use their automakers’ apps to monitor their charging session from afar, but for drivers who don’t want to do even that, it has introduced a new Driver’s Dashboard which can be accessed via a QR code displayed on the charger. The code opens a web portal that tracks the current session, with no download, account or password required.

“So you can walk away and at least see what state of charge your vehicle is in and when your car will be done, or how much power you’re pulling,” Cutler said.

Many partner automakers have begun offering discounts to drivers who use Plug & Charge at Ionna stations.Ionna

Making charging more affordable

Ionna also announced on Wednesday that Hyundai and Mercedes-Benz will soon offer drivers discounted energy rates (around 10% off) through their apps when charging at an Ionna Rechargery via Plug & Charge. The brands join BMW (20%) and GM (10%) in offering their own discounts, with more automakers potentially to come. 

Ionna’s current maximum base rate of 39 cents per kWh (plus applicable taxes) across its entire network is already a pretty good deal compared to competitors charging up to 65 cents per kWh at peak. For context, on my recent EV road trip, a 10-80% charge for a Chevy Equinox EV cost $43.27 at a Tesla Supercharger, while my next 20-80% charge at a Rechargery was just $16.47 without the GM discount.

“We believe at Ionna that our job is to build out a quality-at-scale charging network to unlock adoption of EVs,” Cutler said. “And part of that has to be the affordability of charging, because if it’s too expensive, it totally changes the equation of total cost of ownership of owning an EV versus an internal combustion engine.”

I asked Cutler what more Ionna could be doing for urban drivers who often rely exclusively on public charging — those stuck paying what experts call the “Renters’ Penalty,” spending up to six times more for charging than homeowners who can charge cheaply at home.

“We are piloting time-of-use rates in a couple of locations, and we’re having conversations about expanding that more broadly next year as another tool in our chest,” Cutler said. “We’re finding levers to pull from an affordability standpoint, and we’re not done yet in terms of driving progress there.”

According to the company’s reckoning, that makes Ionna “the largest 400-kilowatt fast charging network in the US,” a very specific claim worth examining.

title: These are my favorite iPhone 18 Pro & Pro Max cases so far [Video]
snippet: The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites! more…
fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites!

Be sure to check out our hands-on video with all of these cases to see which one would be best for you!

Pitaka Edge case

I have always leaned towards ultra-thin and minimal cases. I like being able to protect my iPhone while still feeling its actual design. If thinness and lightweight cases are what you are into then Pitaka’s Edge cases are the first option I would consider. You get:

Ultra-thin and lightweight aramid fiber construction

Improved camera protection with a raised camera lip and PitaTap camera control cover

Built-in MagSafe magnets for added strength

Precise cutouts for the buttons, speakers, and USB-C port

Available in a ton of different designs

Even at just 20g and 1mm in thickness, this case offers a ton of protection and rigidity. Pitaka’s Edge case is available today on Amazon for $59 and comes in 10+ colors and designs. 

Nomad Sport Case

Nomad’s Sport Case gives you that perfect balance of everyday protection while staying relatively thin and lightweight. I went with the Lunar Gret color to contrast with the Deep Black iPhone, and it looks fantastic. This case brings:

Smooth, soft-touch exterior with a protective construction

Tactile metal buttons with a textured finish

Microfiber interior lining to help protect your iPhone

Raised camera and screen edges for additional protection

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and a dedicated Camera Control cover

If you want a high-quality, no-frills case that keeps your phone protected while still making it look awesome, I would look into the Nomad Sport case. It’s available on Amazon for $55!

Xtremm Inno E-Ink Case

This is easily one of the most unique and fun cases that I have ever reviewed. The Xtremm Inno  puts a color E-Ink display on the rear of the iPhone that is 100% customizable. You can put any image you want on there, like family photos, team logos, anime characters, literally anything. It’s all done via NFC, so the case does not need a battery, power, or Bluetooth, keeping it as thin and light as any other regular case. It feels like magic. 

Customizable color E-Ink display on the back of the case

NFC technology for transferring images from your iPhone

Support for personal photos and AI-generated designs

Raised camera protection and dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in MagSafe compatibility despite the rear display

We have a whole video on this to show it off. I recommend watching it before purchasing, just to see how cool this looks! It’s available on Amazon for $75 and comes in five different colors for the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. 

Rokform Crystal Case

Now, if you need something a bit more rugged with added protection but still want to show off that new burgundy iPhone color, then Rokform is a great choice. Not only is it extremely protective, but It Also has Rokform’s proprietary locking system in addition to MagSafe. This makes it even more useful for someone who needs to securely mount their iPhone on a bike, motorcycle, or other devices that require more than just magnets. 

Rugged construction with reinforced corners and raised edges

Transparent back panel that shows off your iPhone’s color

Rokform’s proprietary twist-lock mounting system

Built-in MagSafe compatibility

Full camera plateau protection with a dedicated Camera Control cover

The Rokform Crystal Case is available on Amazon for $69. They also have their own ecosystem of mounts and attachments worth checking out. 

BodyGuardz Weave Case

This is a brand that I had not heard much about until this year. They have been around for a while, but they just released their new Weave line, and I love the design, texture, and multifunctionality of it all. You get:

Textured woven exterior with a comfortable grip

Integrated kickstand 

Speaker channels designed to direct audio forward

Raised edges for screen and camera protection

Built-in MagSafe 

The speaker directional feature is something I had not seen before, and it actually makes a nice difference. Because of how the speaker cutout is designed, it directs the audio right at you rather than to your left or right. Very unique touch! The BodyGuardz Weave is available on Amazon for $59

Andar Aspen

If you are someone who misses the old iPhone leather cases of years past, then Andar is the next best alternative. I have been using their cases for years, and they are some of the best leather cases on the market. You get:

Genuine leather exterior that develops a unique patina over time and smells fantastic 

Soft microfiber interior lining 

Raised edges around the display and camera for additional protection

Dedicated Camera Control cover and tactile metal buttons

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and multiple color options

Their new black color matches the Deep Black iPhone so well that it almost makes the iPhone disappear in the shadows. They have over 10 colors to choose from, and these cases just get better with time. The Andar Aspen Case is available for $70 and can be purchased directly through Andar.

Spigen Nano Pop Case

Spigen’s Nano Pop case is a great option if you are looking for something that will color-match and enhance your new iPhone. It has a two-tone design that looks especially nice with the new Burgundy iPhone, and it also has uniquely textured sides for additional grip in the hand. The Pop case gives you:

Two-tone design with contrasting colors

Flexible, rubberized construction with textured sides for additional grip

Raised edges and protection around the entire camera plateau

Dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in lanyard attachment point

This one is the most budget-friendly of the bunch as well, sitting at just $21 directly from Amazon

Final take

As I mentioned in the intro, cases are highly subjective purchases. It is almost like clothing but for your phone. There is no right or wrong answer to any of these, just a matter of what you think works and looks best. All of these have their own unique selling points and differentiators, and they come from very reputable brands, so there is no going wrong with any of them. I personally like to keep it as thin and light as possible, while I know my brother likes his cases bulky and protective. 

Be sure to catch our video on these, as we go hands-on with all of these cases, and leave a comment on some other brands I need to check out. I would love to give you guys a round two of my favorite cases later in the year. For those people waiting for the iPhone Duo, we will also have something similar for the new device.

title: Blender, the 3D modeling app, is launching for Android next year; iPad app still on pause
snippet: One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android. more…
fullText:
One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android.

Blender is an industry-recognized suite of tools used for 3D modeling. It’s effectively the go-to option, and for good reason. 

Shown off at the Blender Conference 2026, Blender is making the effort to bring its app to Android. The hour-long video goes over the details of how the app works and the roadmap for releasing the port, which is targeting a release in the first half of 2027. An APK demo is already available. The port appears to be mainly focused on tablets, which is a bigger undertaking than you might think. Blender relies quite heavily on keyboard shortcuts, so bringing a fully functional experience on a touchscreen is a massive change. It appears that a stylus is a big part of the experience.

This comes at an important time, not only as Android tablets continue to advance, but also as Googlebook makes its debut. The Android-based platform opens up a new desktop-class platform for Blender.

	

Notably, iPad support for Blender is still “on hold” for the time being, despite the work for touchscreen support being brought to the Android app.

title: Can Air Purifiers Clear Wildfire Smoke From Your Home? What Our Lab Data Reveals
snippet: We’ve found that some are much better at doing so than others.
fullText:
On the morning of June 7, 2023, I walked out of my Brooklyn apartment and noticed the skies were hazier than usual, but I chalked it up to a change in weather and headed to work. When I arrived at my Manhattan office that overlooked the Hudson River, though, I knew this was something very different. 

On a normal day, I’d have a clear view of New Jersey on the other side of the water, but on this day, it was merely a blur. As I inspected the thick fog, it dawned on me: This wasn’t fog at all. It was smoke from wildfires that were raging in Canada. The air quality monitor on my phone’s weather app confirmed it. 

Although there was a thick plume of smoke over the city, I could still see the blue skies peeking through, so I continued to work. But by the end of the day, the sky had turned completely dark with an ominous orange tint. This experience was a first for me, so I was alarmed about having to go back outside to return home, and I wasn’t alone, as people in my office began passing out dust masks. I wasn’t sure if they’d help much, but I took one just in case. 

		

			

Even in the subway system, the smell of smoke was undeniable. I made it home, took my dog for the shortest walk possible, then immediately went inside, opened my laptop and ordered an air purifier. I’ve had one running ever since.

The view from my office window in the morning, left, and the view from the same window at the end of the workday, right.Corin Cesaric-Epple/CNET

A perfect storm  

Although the smoke cleared relatively quickly, and the New York skyline bounced back after two days, not every area is as lucky. Texas and the West Coast are particularly vulnerable to these recurring disasters due to their dry climates and the intensifying effects of climate change. Similarly, the 2023 Canadian wildfires occurred during the country’s driest period since 1980, according to NASA.

Data from the National Interagency Fire Center underscores the increasing threat of wildfires. There were 64,897 wildfires in 2024, a sharp increase compared with 77,850 in 2025. Rising temperatures, reduced rainfall and earlier snowmelt around the world create the ideal setting for wildfires to run rampant. 

These types of statistics can feel overwhelming, and while you largely can’t stop a wildfire from happening, you do have control over the air you breathe indoors. To see if air purifiers can make your home’s air safer and cleaner during wildfire season, we tested more than a dozen models to find out.

Key takeaways: 

According to our exclusive lab data, air purifiers can help clear smoke from a home, but some do significantly better than others.

After testing 18 air purifiers, the Coway 450 was the best overall in our 2026 tests. It had the best overall average results in our particle-removal test and received an Editors’ Choice award.

The Coway 400S was selected as the best air purifier for wildfire smoke because it cleared T90 fine particles in 39 seconds on high fan, earning it a CNET Lab Test award for that performance.

	

			

	

			

									

						Best Air Purifiers of 2026					

							

		

What our testing revealed

To conduct our particle-removal tests at our lab in Louisville, Kentucky, our technicians built a custom smoke chamber to test how quickly an air purifier can remove particulate matter from the air. They created a homemade smoke bomb made from potassium nitrate (KNO3), sucrose (sugar) and sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), then placed it in the smoke chamber along with the unit being tested and a particle counter. 

This test showcases how well each air purifier works at clearing both coarse and fine particles. When determining which unit is best for wildfire smoke, we paid close attention to the fine-particle result, since, according to AirNow, “approximately 90% of total particle mass emitted from wildfires consists of fine particles.”

Fine particles are also the most detrimental to human health because they are tiny, less than or equal to 2.5 microns, so when they are inhaled, they can embed deep into your lungs and cause numerous health issues. 

Our lab data revealed that two Coway air purifiers and one Dreame air purifier especially excelled at clearing fine particles.

The Coway 400S is our top pick for clearing smoke from your home because of its exceptional performance at high fan speed. In our 2026 test, it cleared T90 (the time it took for 90% of particles to be removed) fine particles on high fan in just 39 seconds.

The Coway 450, CNET’s choice for best overall air purifier of 2026, was close to matching the 400S’s performance on high fan, but outperformed it on low fan, taking 1 minute and 53 seconds to remove T90 fine particles.

However, the Dreame Furcatch was the top performer in terms of low fan performance. It cleared T90 fine particles on low fan in 1 minute and 24 seconds, winning a CNET Lab Test award in the process. But it did not perform nearly as well as the Coway options above when set to high fan.

While all three models are great options for different reasons, your choice ultimately depends on how you plan to use the air purifier. 

If you need quick bursts at high fan speed in the event of sudden smoke, go with the Coway 400S. If you prefer a unit that does particularly well on low fan and you plan to always keep it on that setting, opt for the Dreame Furcatch. For the most consistent performance at both high and low fan speeds, the Coway 450 is the best option.

In addition to our particle-removal tests, we also tested energy usage and loudness. The Dyson HushJet earned two CNET Lab Test awards for being the quietest and most energy-efficient option on our list. 

From left to right, the Dreame Furcatch, the Coway 450 and the Levoit 200S-P, three winners from our 2026 air purifier testing. Zooey Liao/CNET/Coway/Dreame/Levoit

Air purifier use in real life

CNET’s wellness editor, Anna Gragert, has experienced wildfires firsthand. In 2025, California’s Eaton Fire forced her to evacuate her apartment, but luckily, it stopped five miles short of her home.

“Despite taping up our window seams before deciding to evacuate, we returned to an apartment that smelled of smoke, and everything was covered in a thin layer of ash,” Gragert says. “We relied on two air purifiers to filter the air and remove the smoke smell, and wouldn’t have been able to comfortably live in our apartment without them after experiencing a wildfire so close to home.”

While an air purifier won’t protect your home from a wildfire and you should always pay close attention to evacuation orders in your area, it can provide an important line of defense if smoke hits your city so you can breathe easier, both figuratively and literally.

title: I Visited Lightship’s AE.1 EV Travel Trailer, and Now I Want to Take an Off-the-Grid Road Trip
snippet: The company, founded by Tesla veterans, is expanding manufacturing in Colorado to keep up with demand from RV enthusiasts.
fullText:
I’m approaching the age where I’m supposed to start desiring RV life. I’m not planning to retire anytime soon, but the older I get, the more appealing the idea of abandoning yard work, home repairs and geographic permanence for a life on the open road in a big old house on wheels becomes. My neighbors have an RV they park in the space between our houses, keeping both a permanent location and a home they can travel in; they still have yard work and house repairs, but few complaints.

So it was with some curiosity that I visited a pop-up for Lightship, a Colorado company making EV trailers for RV enthusiasts, outside the flagship Yeti outdoor-recreation store in Austin, Texas. The company’s eye-catching AE.1 trailer was parked and open to the public. (AE.1 refers to Aero-Electric 1.)

The Lightship AE.1 includes lots of modern design touches, like a kitchen area with a two-burner stove, a fridge and freezer, microwave and a hidden compact dishwasher.Omar L. Gallaga for CNET

Lightship staffers handed out brochures, stickers and pins to visitors who climbed into the trailer, some of whom seemed surprised by the sleek, air-conditioned interior. The demo model boasted a cushioned lounge area, appliances including a hideaway dishwasher, microwave, full sink and stovetop, a full bathroom and shower area, and plenty of storage. It can sleep up to six.

			

More from CNET

The selling point of the highly customizable AE.1, which starts at $157,500, is that it offers a more modern design than most RVs and trailers. It includes thoughtful design touches and an electric-powered motor called TrekDrive that kicks in when in motion to lighten the load on whatever’s pulling the trailer. If it’s an EV truck or SUV, that could significantly extend the range between charges.

Pushing back on decades of RV design

Ben Parker, Lightship’s co-founder and chief commercial officer, worked at Tesla in California as a battery engineer and was inspired while traveling in an RV during the pandemic. Parker started the company with Toby Krauss, another former Tesla employee who worked in finance and product management and serves as Lightship’s CEO.

Parker said there’s a gigantic market of Americans who want to travel in camper RVs, but their options have been limited to a few highly consolidated manufacturers offering unchanging designs. So far, he said, customers interested in Lightship are a mix of EV owners and longtime enthusiasts who want “greater capacity, comfort and independence.”

“Our customers are people who love spending time outdoors and want more freedom in how they travel,” Parker said.

Ben Parker, chief commercial officer and co-founder of Lightship, stands next to the company’s AE.1 EV camper trailer at a pop-up event in Austin, Texas on Sept. 26, 2026.Omar L. Gallaga for CNET

The AE.1’s most notable design feature is that it compresses from a 10-foot-tall Camp Mode with lots of windows and headroom to a Road Mode that lowers the roof to under 7 feet, making the AE.1 more aerodynamic in motion. Most of the trailer’s features, from the lighting to extras like an auto-leveling system and a motorized awning, are controlled by an app. A solar array on the trailer’s roof helps keep power flowing. 

If you limit your A/C and power use, the AE.1 can last for about a week off the grid before it needs additional charging, Parker said. The AE.1 has hookups for EV charging as well as the kind of 220-volt hookups found at RV parks. It can hook up to external devices with vehicle-to-load power capabilities.

Some of the more interesting option features include a pull-down bed that attaches to the trailer’s ceiling and a setup for a 4K video projector that can be mounted inside the trailer for viewing on a pull-down screen. 

“The demand we’ve seen reflects a broader appetite for innovation in the RV space,” Parker said. “Customers are excited by the idea of an RV that combines modern technology, energy independence and a dramatically improved towing experience in a single product.”

The co-founder said his company wants the buying and using experience of an AE.1 to wow customers enough for Lightship to gain a foothold in a market that’s not very open to newcomers.

“Breaking into any established industry requires earning trust,” he said. “We’ve focused on building a high-quality product that solves real customer pain points and delivering an experience that people can immediately appreciate once they see it and use it for themselves.”

New trailer players

Lightship is headquartered in Broomfield, Colorado. It’s expanding its manufacturing center there to accommodate additional trailer production, as well as production of a carriage-minus-trailer product called PowerSled, which it’s been selling to businesses like movie productions that need a mobile platform with electric power.

Lightship’s mission to disrupt the RV market is not unlike that of another company, Pebble, that has also been making EV trailers in California.

Parker said the main difference between Lightship and Pebble is that Lightship is sourcing more of its materials domestically. Parker estimates that about 75% of the materials used to make an AE.1 are sourced domestically, and all assembly is done in-house.

Pebble, however, is undercutting Lightship on price. Lightship originally planned to offer a lower-priced $125,000 base model without the self-propelled TrekDrive motor. However, the company has since changed its strategy, moving to a single standard base price with a standard 77 kWh battery and various add-on options and upgrades.

Possible retirement plans

For me, a non-RV person, the AE.1 feels design-forward and includes features like a built-in auto-hitch, an auto-leveler, and lots of charging ports and stations, all of which appeal to someone like me who has no idea what they’re doing. The interior feels spacious, but not so much that it makes the exterior look oversized. The ability to shrink down to a smaller size — the AE.1 performs safety checks before compressing to ensure windows aren’t open and nothing will break — brings the wow factor.

It doesn’t take much time in the trailer to imagine traveling in it and using Lightship’s trailer as a mobile workstation (satellite internet service is not included, but it can be hooked up).

The AE.1 isn’t cheap, but it might be worth putting on the retirement wish list. You will still have to wait: the company’s waitlist for delivery is currently about a year long.

Lightship began shipping AE.1 trailers last year and said it expects to produce about 30 over the rest of this year. By sometime in 2027, with its expanded factory floor, it plans to ramp that up to 40 per month.

If you want to check out the AE.1 for yourself, the company maintains showrooms north of Denver and in San Francisco and will host a pop-up event in Las Vegas in late November.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Omar Gallaga
						

						

											

								

											Omar Gallaga has covered technology, digital culture and other topics for outlets including CNET, NPR, WIRED, Texas Monthly, MSNBC, Consumer Reports, The Washington Post, the Los Angeles Times, The Atlantic and the Austin American-Statesman, where he was a longtime tech reporter, editor and podcaster. He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

title: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Simplifies Streaming Options, and I Went Hands-On
snippet: The 2026 streamer from Amazon features a new remote and support for HDR10 and Samsung’s HDR10 Plus.
fullText:
Amazon has unveiled a new Fire TV Stick 4K as part of a simplified lineup for the popular streamers, and it has 4K HDR10 playback.

The $60 Fire TV Stick 4K, which replaces both the Fire TV Stick 4K Select and 4K Plus, comes with a new remote and support for HDR10 and Samsung’s HDR10 Plus. It has 8GB internal storage, a quad-core 1.7 GHz processor and support for Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3 and Bluetooth Low Energy. The company says the Stick 4K is 20% to 40% faster than the similarly priced Roku Streaming Stick Plus.

While it’s not consequential, as it’s going to spend all of its time behind your TV, the Fire TV Stick 4K feels solid in the hand. It seems much more luxe than any other Fire TV Stick I’ve ever used. The device comes with a USB cable, and it no longer needs to be plugged into the wall; it can be powered by your TV’s USB port.

The new remote no longer has a dedicated Alexa button.

I found the “upgraded” experience extends to the redesigned remote, which, unusually, no longer includes a prominent blue Alexa button. Instead, the most obvious button features a bright red home icon, and the microphone is now relegated to the top right.

Amazon also said that a new premium remote is coming in 2027, which features backlighting and a “find my remote” feature.

The streaming device is designed to be used in conjunction with Alexa Plus, and one impressive feature the representatives showed me was the forthcoming ability to plug articles into the app. They showed me how to load a “10 best movies about…” article into the Fire TV app and have the TV add the movies listed to a watch-next list.

The Fire TV Stick 4K home screenTy Pendlebury/CNET

In general, the setup and use of the Fire TV Stick 4K felt very familiar, but since it was fresh out of the box, I didn’t notice any blazing speeds. This will likely improve over time as the device learns the apps I use most.

The best part about the Fire TV Stick 4K’s release, however, is the simplification of the range for buyers, and this stick should now be the go-to device for most people. Enthusiasts who want to make the most of their home cinema should get the $85 4K Max model for Dolby Vision and Atmos, or support for add-on speakers via Alexa Home Theater.

The range is now just four main devices:

Fire TV Stick HD $40

Fire TV Stick 4K $60

Fire TV Stick 4K Max $85

Fire TV Cube $199

The Fire TV Stick 4K is available now for an introductory price of $30, and this will likely continue until Amazon Prime Big Deal Days next week.

title: This Might Be the Only Hair Straightening Tool You Need
snippet: It’s super lightweight and delivers more impressive results than you’d expect for its size.
fullText:
CNET’s key takeaways

The Bluvol I11 Apex cordless hair straightening comb retails for $90.

The I11 Apex is a perfect travel companion for easy touch-ups.

You’ll get up to 45 minutes of styling per charge.

After more than 10 years of wearing my natural curls, I started straightening my hair again. I spent countless hours searching for the best tools and products that would deliver sleek, frizz-free results while protecting my hair from heat damage. The Tymo Ring hair straightening brush stood out to me, and it’s been a good addition to my hair care kit. However, it may have just been replaced by the Bluvol I11 Apex cordless straightening comb.

When the Bluvol I11 Apex arrived, I wasn’t expecting much. I figured it would be good for the occasional touch-up on travel days or even quick fixes if I ever got caught in the rain, but it proved me wrong. It’s lightweight and fits nicely in the hand. From holding it, you can tell it’s well-made. I just couldn’t imagine that something that compact could pack so much heat. 

What the Bluvol I11 Apex looks like straight out of the box.

Putting the Bluvol I11 Apex to the test

To really put the Bluvol I11 Apex to the test, I enlisted my cousin’s help. She’s Gen Z, an expert at all things hair and nails, and most importantly, she has an amazing, thick head of hair. After unboxing the straightening comb, I charged it, and we got started. 

			

More from CNET

It has three heat settings: 320, 365 and 410 degrees Fahrenheit. There’s an LCD screen, which shows the temperature and battery percentage. Switching to a lower or higher setting is simple, using the power button. Once you’ve chosen your temperature, the display will blink as the comb heats up. When it stops blinking, you’re ready to go.

On the first pass, we were impressed with how effortlessly it took my cousin’s hair from curly to straight. The I11 Apex has upgraded ceramic glazed plates throughout the teeth of the comb, which prevent singes and allow multiple passes without damage. Its wide heating area provides even heat distribution for consistent coverage across strands. 

Bluvol says the straightener releases “200 million negative ions to smooth hair and reduce static and frizz.” While I can’t test that accurately, I can attest that it left her hair far smoother than a similar flat iron and required fewer passes to achieve the desired results.

The results on curly hair.

Battery life and charging time

Bluvol includes a charging cable and suggests using a 15-watt or higher adapter when powering up. With the adapter, you’ll go from zero to a full charge in about 2.5 hours. A full charge will give you up to 45 minutes of styling time. We managed to make it about 80% of the way through her hair before needing to recharge.

Who’s the Bluvol I11 Apex for?

This is by far the most impressive cordless straightener I’ve tested, but it might not be for everyone. For folks with shorter hair, this won’t be ideal because the layout of the comb’s teeth doesn’t allow it to really hold super short strands to straighten. The company also notes that if your hair is “very curly,” you might need to use professional styling products for the best results. 

The I11 Apex is the perfect styling companion for when you’re on the go. There are no wires, so you never have to search for an outlet. It’s easy to slip into your handbag, backpack or luggage. There’s even a physical lock switch that prevents it from turning on while it’s stashed away.

Price

This straightening comb typically retails for $90, but Amazon is currently offering a 22% discount for Prime Members.

The specs

Price: $90 retail, but often on sale for less

Battery life: 45 minutes

Wattage: 33 watts

Estimated charge time: 2.5 hours from 0 to 100 with a 15-watt adapter

Number of ports: 1 USB-C port

Max temperature: 410 degrees Fahrenheit (210 degrees Celsius)

Weight: 1.46 pounds

CNET’s buying advice

Whether you want effortless touch-ups on the go or a full straightening solution at home, the Bluvol I11 Apex can get the job done. Want the best of both worlds? Tymo has a new two-in-one straightening brush with a built-in traditional flat iron. If you don’t need the portably of I11 Apex, then it’s worth considering.
